evidence.explanation: GeneReviews describes genetic counseling and testing options for at-risk relatives in PLOD1-kEDS.

treatments/3.description: Genetic counseling regarding autosomal recessive inheritance, recurrence risk, and availability of carrier and prenatal/preimplantation testing.

evidence.snippet: Functional studies showed that the p.R316Q, p.S219F, and p.R322Q variants render the FTO protein inactive.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that three of the reported catalytic-domain alleles inactivate the protein in the same assay. Note the sentence writes p.S219F where the variant reported elsewhere in the same abstract is p.S319F.

evidence.snippet: Loss-of-function resulting from the patient's R96P missense variant was demonstrated with in vitro biochemical characterization of demethylase activity, resulting in a 90% reduction in function of the fat mass and obesity-associated protein compared to wild-type.
evidence.explanation: Shows that an allele outside the catalytic site reaches the same functional endpoint, which is why this node is defined by loss of activity rather than by domain location.

steps/1.description: Five homozygous missense alleles have been reported: R316Q, S319F, R322Q and H271P in the catalytic domain, and R96P in the substrate-recognition lid outside the catalytic site. Four of the five have been characterised biochemically and reduce or abolish FTO demethylase activity, so the characterised alleles converge on the same molecular consequence from two different parts of the protein. H271P has not been assayed for demethylase activity in the report describing it; the case for it rests on homozygosity in a consanguineous patient, absence from population databases, and its location in the catalytic domain.

evidence.snippet: Biochemical studies reveal that p.(Ser319Phe) FTO has reduced 2-oxoglutarate turnover and N-methyl-nucleoside demethylase activity.
evidence.explanation: Measures both the cosubstrate turnover and the demethylase output for a second disease allele.

evidence.snippet: We report here that fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) has efficient oxidative demethylation activity targeting the abundant N6-methyladenosine (m(6)A) residues in RNA in vitro.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the substrate that later reports assay. Cited to establish the substrate ambiguity described on this node rather than to make a claim about the disease; this paper is not about the malformation syndrome.

steps/2.description: FTO is an Fe(II)- and 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase of the AlkB family. Which of its substrates matters for this disease is not established: the 2009 index report assayed 3-methylthymidine turnover in single-stranded DNA, predating the identification of FTO as the first mRNA m6A demethylase, while the 2023 report assayed m6A. No study has shown which activity the malformation phenotype depends on.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that loss of Fto leads to developmental defects such as growth retardation, craniofacial dysmorphism and aberrant neural crest cells migration in Zebrafish.
evidence.explanation: The developmental phenotype in the zebrafish model, which is the closest any model comes to the human malformation syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Canonical Wnt signalling is down regulated by abrogated β-Catenin translocation to the nucleus whilst non-canonical Wnt/Ca(2+) pathway is activated via its key signal mediators CaMKII and PKCδ.
evidence.explanation: The directional Wnt result behind the two Wnt process bindings on this node. Graded IN_VITRO because this sentence reports the Fto-null MEF and HEK293T work; the zebrafish arm is graded separately above.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, we demonstrate that loss of Fto results in short, absent or disorganised cilia leading to situs inversus, renal cystogenesis, neural crest cell defects and microcephaly in Zebrafish.
evidence.explanation: The ciliary result and the organ phenotypes it is said to produce, including microcephaly, which is also a human phenotype in this entry.

steps/3.description: Loss of Fto shifts the balance between the two branches of Wnt signalling - canonical signalling falls because beta-catenin fails to translocate to the nucleus, while the non-canonical Wnt/calcium branch is activated through CaMKII and PKC-delta - and produces short, absent or disorganised cilia. In zebrafish this is accompanied by growth retardation, craniofacial dysmorphism, aberrant neural crest cell migration, microcephaly, situs inversus and renal cystogenesis, and Fto knockout mice show tissue-specific ciliary abnormality. This is the only worked-out route from FTO loss to a developmental phenotype, and it has been shown only in model systems: no patient tissue has been examined for either the Wnt shift or the ciliary defect.

evidence.snippet: Cultured skin fibroblasts from affected subjects showed impaired proliferation and accelerated senescence.
evidence.explanation: The original cellular result, from the index pedigree.

evidence.snippet: Although we did not test senescence, we were not able to detect any abnormalities in either morphology or proliferation in the patient fibroblast cultures compared to either parent or control fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: A direct negative result on the proliferation and morphology arm in a second patient's fibroblasts, with parental controls. REFUTE applies to proliferation and morphology only; the same sentence states senescence was not tested, which is why the senescence claim rests on the index report alone.

steps/4.description: Cultured skin fibroblasts from the index family showed impaired proliferation and accelerated senescence. A later patient's fibroblasts showed no difference in morphology, proliferation or apoptosis against parental and unrelated controls; that report did not test senescence. The two results are not reconciled, and the second patient also carried a nonsense CETP variant, so this node is retained with both results attached rather than treated as an established step.

evidence.snippet: These findings indicate that FTO is essential for normal development of the central nervous and cardiovascular systems in human and establish that a mutation in a human member of the AlkB-related dioxygenase family results in a severe polymalformation syndrome.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own conclusion, quoted here for its central-nervous-system half; the cardiovascular half of the same sentence is quoted on the Failure of cardiovascular development node. Note it is an inference from phenotype, not a mechanism.

evidence.snippet: All cases appeared to have a severe CNS phenotype. Ventriculomegaly and cortical atrophy were common to both this patient and prior cases.
evidence.explanation: The cross-family statement that the neurological arm is severe and that two specific findings recur, which is what justifies asserting an organ-system node rather than a single-patient observation.

steps/5.description: The neurological arm of the index report's conclusion, drawn from the pattern of malformations rather than from a demonstrated developmental mechanism. Nothing published fills in the steps between loss of demethylase activity and a lissencephalic cortex or a posterior fossa anomaly, and this entry does not invent them. The node is asserted at the level of "development of this organ system fails", which is why every edge leaving it is INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES.

evidence.snippet: These findings indicate that FTO is essential for normal development of the central nervous and cardiovascular systems in human and establish that a mutation in a human member of the AlkB-related dioxygenase family results in a severe polymalformation syndrome.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own conclusion, quoted here for its cardiovascular half. Note it is an inference from phenotype, not a mechanism.

evidence.snippet: The affected family members suffered from postnatal growth retardation, head and face dysmorphisms, severe psychomotor delay, functional cognitive deficits, and, in some patients, brain malformations, cardiac defects, genital abnormalities, and cleft palates.
evidence.explanation: Records cardiac defects in the index pedigree, in some rather than all affected members, which is the observational basis for a cardiovascular node distinct from the neurological one.

steps/6.description: The cardiovascular arm of the same conclusion, and an inference from the malformations observed rather than a demonstrated mechanism: no study connects loss of FTO demethylase activity to a septation or outflow-tract defect. The lesions reported across the families are heterogeneous - septal defects, a patent ductus, a hypoplastic mitral valve, an abnormal aortic arch, anomalous pulmonary venous return and ventricular hypertrophy - with no single characteristic lesion. Curated separately from the neurological node because the two arms dissociate in the models: the zebrafish reproduces part of the neurological phenotype and none of this one.

evidence.snippet: The affected family members suffered from postnatal growth retardation, head and face dysmorphisms, severe psychomotor delay, functional cognitive deficits, and, in some patients, brain malformations, cardiac defects, genital abnormalities, and cleft palates.
evidence.explanation: Postnatal growth retardation as a feature of the index pedigree, named first in the list of what the affected family members had.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that the loss of Fto in mice leads to postnatal growth retardation and a significant reduction in adipose tissue and lean body mass.
evidence.explanation: Growth retardation in the Fto-null mouse, which reproduces this node and not the malformation nodes.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that loss of Fto leads to developmental defects such as growth retardation, craniofacial dysmorphism and aberrant neural crest cells migration in Zebrafish.
evidence.explanation: Growth retardation is the first developmental defect named in the fish, so the two models agree on this arm even though they disagree on the malformations.

steps/7.description: Growth failure begins before birth and is the one arm of the human phenotype that both animal models reproduce, including the Fto-null mouse, which shows no malformation at all. That dissociation is why growth is curated as its own organism-scale node rather than as a consequence of the neurological or cardiovascular malformations. What connects loss of demethylase activity to reduced growth is not established in any system.

evidence.snippet: We investigated a 21-month-old girl who presented distinctive facial features, failure to thrive, global developmental delay, left ventricular cardiac hypertrophy, reduced vision and bilateral hearing loss.
evidence.explanation: Records failure to thrive in the second reported family.

evidence.snippet: The affected family members suffered from postnatal growth retardation, head and face dysmorphisms, severe psychomotor delay, functional cognitive deficits, and, in some patients, brain malformations, cardiac defects, genital abnormalities, and cleft palates.
evidence.explanation: A later paper's summary of the index pedigree's phenotype, cited because the index report's own abstract does not enumerate features. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL because the sentence reports clinical findings in patients.

steps/8.description: Severe postnatal growth failure, present in every reported patient and one of the three features in the OMIM entry title.

evidence.snippet: We investigated a 21-month-old girl who presented distinctive facial features, failure to thrive, global developmental delay, left ventricular cardiac hypertrophy, reduced vision and bilateral hearing loss.
evidence.explanation: Records global developmental delay in the second reported family.

steps/9.description: Severe psychomotor delay with cognitive deficit, reported in every family.

evidence.snippet: Here, we describe a patient born of consanguineous union who presented with microcephaly, developmental delay, behavioral abnormalities, dysmorphic facial features, hypotonia and other various phenotypic abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Records dysmorphic facial features in a fourth reported patient.

steps/10.description: A coarse facial gestalt with distinctive features, described as head and face dysmorphism in the index pedigree.

evidence.snippet: Here, we describe a patient born of consanguineous union who presented with microcephaly, developmental delay, behavioral abnormalities, dysmorphic facial features, hypotonia and other various phenotypic abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Records microcephaly in a reported patient.

steps/11.description: Reduced head circumference, reported with the CNS malformations.

evidence.snippet: On examination, she was hypertonic and lacked the ability to control her head movements.
evidence.explanation: The direct examination finding in this patient, from the paper's own case description.

evidence.snippet: Similar to the FTO phenotype previously reported by Boissel et al., our patient also demonstrated intrauterine growth retardation, failure to thrive, hypertonicity, seizures, severe developmental delay, postnatal microbrachycephaly, dysmorphic craniofacium, sensory-neural hearing loss, and optic disc abnormality, a short neck, cutis marmorata, a PDA, drumstick fingers, brachydactyly.
evidence.explanation: The authors align hypertonicity with the index pedigree, which is the basis for treating increased rather than decreased tone as the recurrent finding.

steps/12.description: Increased muscle tone. This is the better-supported tone abnormality in the families where it was examined directly: the fourth reported patient was described on examination as hypertonic, and the same paper's discussion lists hypertonicity among the features it shares with the index pedigree.

evidence.snippet: She remained in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) for 2 months postpartum due to hypotonia, respiratory failure, and poor feeding.
evidence.explanation: Hypotonia in the first sibling of the Yemeni family, reported in a later paper's summary of that case.

evidence.snippet: Her 1-year follow-up disclosed multiple abnormal physical features (see Table 1), and truncal hypotonia with mild spasticity of upper and lower extremities.
evidence.explanation: The second sibling, with both reduced axial tone and limb spasticity, which is why the description says tone abnormality is not consistently in one direction.

steps/13.description: Reduced muscle tone. Tone abnormality in this disease is not consistently in one direction: hypotonia is reported in the two siblings of the third family, one of them as truncal hypotonia with limb spasticity, while the fourth patient was examined as hypertonic. Both are curated because both are reported.

evidence.snippet: All cases appeared to have a severe CNS phenotype. Ventriculomegaly and cortical atrophy were common to both this patient and prior cases.
evidence.explanation: The cross-family statement that the CNS phenotype is severe and that two specific findings recur.

evidence.snippet: The affected family members suffered from postnatal growth retardation, head and face dysmorphisms, severe psychomotor delay, functional cognitive deficits, and, in some patients, brain malformations, cardiac defects, genital abnormalities, and cleft palates.
evidence.explanation: Records brain malformations in the index pedigree, in some rather than all affected members. Same sentence used for other index-pedigree features, so the evidence_source is unchanged.

steps/14.description: Structural brain malformation is a consistent and severe feature. Ventriculomegaly and cortical atrophy recur across the reported families; the fifth patient had a Dandy-Walker spectrum anomaly with hydrocephalus, a thin cortical mantle and severe parenchymal loss, and the second patient had decreased brain parenchyma with delayed myelination and a thin corpus callosum.

evidence.snippet: The patient’s magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain was notable for Dandy-Walker malformation, hydrocephalus, a thin cortical mantle, and severe loss of the underlying parenchyma
evidence.explanation: The postnatal MRI finding in this patient.

steps/15.description: A Dandy-Walker spectrum anomaly with an incompletely rotated vermis, large foramen of Magendie and large cisterna magna was detected prenatally in the fifth reported patient and confirmed on postnatal MRI. Reported in one patient, so no frequency is implied.

evidence.snippet: Third ventriculostomy and choroid plexus cauterization were undertaken for management of the hydrocephalus.
evidence.explanation: Records the hydrocephalus and the fact that it required surgical management.

steps/16.description: Hydrocephalus accompanied the Dandy-Walker anomaly in the fifth patient and required third ventriculostomy and choroid plexus cauterization.

evidence.snippet: All cases appeared to have a severe CNS phenotype. Ventriculomegaly and cortical atrophy were common to both this patient and prior cases.
evidence.explanation: Names ventriculomegaly as recurrent across the reported families rather than as a single-patient finding.

steps/17.description: Progressive ventriculomegaly, described as one of the two brain findings common to this patient and the earlier cases.

evidence.snippet: The affected family members suffered from postnatal growth retardation, head and face dysmorphisms, severe psychomotor delay, functional cognitive deficits, and, in some patients, brain malformations, cardiac defects, genital abnormalities, and cleft palates.
evidence.explanation: Records cardiac defects, and notes they were present in some rather than all members of the index pedigree.

steps/18.description: Cardiac defects were reported in some members of the index pedigree, and left ventricular hypertrophy in a later patient. No single lesion is characteristic across the reported families.

evidence.snippet: We investigated a 21-month-old girl who presented distinctive facial features, failure to thrive, global developmental delay, left ventricular cardiac hypertrophy, reduced vision and bilateral hearing loss.
evidence.explanation: Records left ventricular hypertrophy in a single reported patient.

steps/19.description: Reported in the second family's patient. It is one patient, so no frequency is implied.

evidence.snippet: Pregnancy was complicated by multiple fetal anomalies in diverse systems as follows: (1) uterine environmental (polyhydramnios, intrauterine growth restriction (estimated fetal weight <1%), umbilical cord thickening with increased volume of Wharton’s jelly, and elevated uterine artery Doppler indices with preserved diastolic flow); (2) central nervous system (CNS; poor gyral development, small cerebral hemispheres, and Dandy-Walker spectrum anomaly with incompletely rotated vermis, large foramen of Magendie, large cisterna magna, and hydrocephalus); (3) musculoskeletal (all long bones <5% mean for gestational age without evidence of fracture, thoracic cage 9% mean for gestational age, and disorganized anterior maxillary tooth buds); and (4) cardiovascular (ventricular septal defect, hypoplastic mitral valve, and aortic arch) (Table 1).
evidence.explanation: The fetal anomaly survey for this patient; item (4) enumerates the cardiovascular lesions, of which the ventricular septal defect is one.

steps/20.description: A ventricular septal defect was one of the prenatally detected cardiovascular anomalies in the fifth reported patient, alongside a hypoplastic mitral valve and an abnormal aortic arch. Reported in one patient, so no frequency band is given.

evidence.snippet: Postnatal echocardiographic evaluation showed a secundum atrial septal defect, a patent foramen ovale, three pulmonary veins entering the left atrium, and predominant right-to-left flow with reversal of flow through the aortic arch.
evidence.explanation: The postnatal echocardiogram, which names the defect as a secundum atrial septal defect rather than an unspecified one.

steps/21.description: Postnatal echocardiography in the fifth reported patient showed a secundum atrial septal defect together with a patent foramen ovale and anomalous pulmonary venous return. Reported in one patient.

evidence.snippet: Similar to the FTO phenotype previously reported by Boissel et al., our patient also demonstrated intrauterine growth retardation, failure to thrive, hypertonicity, seizures, severe developmental delay, postnatal microbrachycephaly, dysmorphic craniofacium, sensory-neural hearing loss, and optic disc abnormality, a short neck, cutis marmorata, a PDA, drumstick fingers, brachydactyly.
evidence.explanation: Lists a PDA among the shared features, which is the only lesion-level cardiac description available for this patient.

steps/22.description: A patent ductus arteriosus was among the features the fourth reported patient shared with the index pedigree.

evidence.snippet: The patient was intubated for respiratory failure and pulmonary hypertension.
evidence.explanation: The presenting indication for intubation in this patient.

evidence.snippet: She continued to have severe pulmonary hypertension requiring ventilatory support.
evidence.explanation: Records that the pulmonary hypertension was severe and persistent rather than a transient neonatal finding.

steps/23.description: Severe pulmonary hypertension in the fifth reported patient required intubation at birth and continued ventilatory support, with right-to-left shunting and reversed aortic arch flow. The report does not subclassify it hemodynamically, so the general elevated-pulmonary-artery-pressure term is bound rather than a pre- or post-capillary child term.

evidence.snippet: The affected family members suffered from postnatal growth retardation, head and face dysmorphisms, severe psychomotor delay, functional cognitive deficits, and, in some patients, brain malformations, cardiac defects, genital abnormalities, and cleft palates.
evidence.explanation: Records cleft palate as an in-some-patients feature of the index pedigree.

steps/24.description: Reported in some members of the index pedigree.

evidence.snippet: We further expand on the phenotype of homozygous FTO loss-of-function mutations to include eye abnormalities, gingival overgrowth, craniosynostosis, and cutaneous photosensitivity.
evidence.explanation: The report that added craniosynostosis to the phenotype.

steps/25.description: Added to the phenotype by the third family's report, together with gingival overgrowth and photosensitivity.

evidence.snippet: Similar to the FTO phenotype previously reported by Boissel et al., our patient also demonstrated intrauterine growth retardation, failure to thrive, hypertonicity, seizures, severe developmental delay, postnatal microbrachycephaly, dysmorphic craniofacium, sensory-neural hearing loss, and optic disc abnormality, a short neck, cutis marmorata, a PDA, drumstick fingers, brachydactyly.
evidence.explanation: Names intrauterine growth retardation as a feature shared with the index pedigree.

steps/26.description: Growth failure begins before birth: the fourth reported patient had intrauterine growth retardation, and the fifth had an estimated fetal weight below the first centile on the prenatal anomaly survey.

evidence.snippet: Our findings demonstrate a novel fat mass and obesity-associated gene non-catalytic site variant with a unique patient phenotype of bilateral multifocal epilepsy and multisystem congenital anomalies.
evidence.explanation: Records the epilepsy, and the authors' own framing of it as unique to that patient rather than characteristic of the disease.

steps/27.description: Bilateral multifocal epilepsy was reported in the 2023 patient carrying the non-catalytic-site allele, and is described there as a novel feature.

edges/1.description: Each reported allele reduces or abolishes the enzyme's catalytic output.

edges/2.description: The one mechanistic route between loss of FTO and a developmental phenotype that has been worked out, though only in model systems.

edges/3.description: The one cellular phenotype reported for patient cells, and the one that a later report failed to reproduce.

edges/4.description: The index report concludes that FTO is essential for development of the central nervous system, on the basis of the malformations observed.

edges/5.description: The same conclusion for the cardiovascular system. Curated as a separate node because the two organ systems fail independently in the reported patients and because the models diverge on them.

edges/6.description: Growth failure is the arm of the human phenotype both animal models reproduce, and it is not downstream of either malformation node: it starts before birth and is present in animals with no malformation at all.

edges/7.description: Proposed route to the human brain malformations. The link is drawn from model systems only; no patient tissue has been examined for either the Wnt shift or the ciliary defect.

edges/8.description: Craniofacial dysmorphism and aberrant neural crest cell migration are the two developmental phenotypes this node was defined by in the fish, and the coarse facial gestalt is the human feature they correspond to most directly.

edges/9.description: The palatal shelves are built by cranial neural crest, whose migration is aberrant in the Fto-deficient fish. Cleft palate is reported in some members of the index pedigree; the connection to the neural crest defect is an inference from the model, not a result in patients.

edges/10.description: Premature suture fusion, added to the phenotype by the third family's report. Drawn from this node on the grounds that the cranial vault and its sutures form at the boundary between neural crest and paraxial mesoderm under Wnt control; no study has examined sutures in an FTO-deficient animal, so this is an inference from the model rather than a result.

edges/11.description: Disturbed CNS development presents as severe psychomotor delay.

edges/12.description: Reduced brain growth is part of the CNS phenotype.

edges/13.description: Structural brain malformation is the direct morphological expression of failed central nervous system development, and ventriculomegaly and cortical atrophy are named as recurrent across the reported families.

edges/14.description: A posterior fossa malformation, detected prenatally and confirmed on MRI in the fifth patient. Which step of hindbrain development fails is not known.

edges/15.description: Reported with the Dandy-Walker anomaly in the same patient and requiring surgical management. The reports do not separate hydrocephalus arising from the posterior fossa malformation from hydrocephalus arising independently, so it is drawn from the organ-system node rather than from the Dandy-Walker phenotype.

edges/16.description: One of the two brain findings named as common to this patient and the earlier cases.

edges/17.description: Epilepsy in the patient with the most severe cortical malformation, a thin cortical mantle with poor gyral development. No study has shown the epilepsy to be a consequence of the malformation rather than a parallel effect of losing FTO, so the edge is drawn at the organ-system level and no intermediate is claimed.

edges/18.description: Reduced axial tone of central origin, reported in the two siblings of the third family.

edges/19.description: Increased tone with limb spasticity, the tone abnormality recorded on direct examination in the fourth patient. Tone abnormality in this disease runs in both directions and both directions are drawn from this node.

edges/20.description: Cardiac malformation follows from disturbed cardiovascular development.

edges/21.description: Failure of ventricular septation, on the prenatal anomaly survey in the fifth patient.

edges/22.description: Failure of atrial septation, on postnatal echocardiography in the same patient.

edges/23.description: Failure of the ductus arteriosus to close, listed among the features the fourth patient shared with the index pedigree.

edges/24.description: Reported in the second family's patient. Whether this is a primary myocardial abnormality or a response to another lesion in the same heart is not established in any report, so it is drawn from the organ-system node without a claimed intermediate.

edges/25.description: Severe and persistent in the patient who also had anomalous pulmonary venous return, right-to-left shunting and reversed aortic arch flow. That same patient had severe tracheobronchomalacia and respiratory failure, and no report separates the contribution of the structural cardiovascular anomalies from that of the airway and lung disease, which is why no intermediate is claimed.

edges/26.description: Growth failure is already present prenatally: the fourth patient had intrauterine growth retardation and the fifth an estimated fetal weight below the first centile.

edges/27.description: Severe postnatal growth failure, present in every reported patient. The route from demethylase loss to growth failure is not established.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that a R316Q mutation, inactivating FTO enzymatic activity, is responsible for an autosomal-recessive lethal syndrome.
evidence.explanation: The founding gene-disease claim.

evidence.snippet: We identified a novel FTO homozygous missense mutation (c.956C>T; p.(Ser319Phe)) in the affected individual.
evidence.explanation: The second independent family, which is what moved the relationship beyond a single pedigree.

genes/0.notes: ClinGen has no gene-disease validity assertion for FTO in the gene-validity snapshot cached in this repository, so no CGGV record is cited; the four disagreeing GenCC submissions are recorded in external_assertions instead. The controlled functional-impact value is carried on the pathophysiology node's genetic_context block.

evidence.snippet: She spent 1 month in the NICU for poor feeding and required nasogastric feeds on discharge.
evidence.explanation: A reported instance of the supportive, organ-directed management this umbrella entry describes - nutritional support for poor feeding, continued after discharge. No publication describes a management protocol for this disease, so the entry is anchored to a reported instance rather than to a recommendation.

treatments/0.description: No disease-modifying treatment exists and none has been proposed, and no interventional trial has been registered for this disease. Management is supportive and organ-directed. The specific interventions that have actually been reported in patients are curated as separate entries below rather than being named only in this entry's prose.

evidence.snippet: The patient underwent multiple failed extubations, ultimately leading to tracheostomy.
evidence.explanation: Records both the tracheostomy and the failed-extubation course that led to it.

evidence.snippet: Airway evaluation documented severe tracheobronchomalacia.
evidence.explanation: The airway lesion behind the extubation failures, and the reason a tracheostomy rather than continued intubation was needed.

treatments/1.description: The fifth reported patient had severe tracheobronchomalacia and failed repeated extubation, and was managed with a tracheostomy. This is a response to that patient's airway disease, not an established standard of care for the syndrome; it is reported in one patient.

evidence.snippet: She continued to have severe pulmonary hypertension requiring ventilatory support.
evidence.explanation: States the indication for continued ventilatory support in this patient.

evidence.snippet: The patient has since been discharged home tracheostomy and is ventilator dependent.
evidence.explanation: Records that the ventilation became long-term rather than an acute intensive-care measure.

treatments/2.description: Ventilatory support was required for the fifth patient's severe pulmonary hypertension and was not weaned; she was discharged home ventilator dependent. Reported in one patient.

evidence.snippet: During her hospitalization she began to have seizures that were managed with antiepileptic medications.
evidence.explanation: Antiepileptic treatment in the fourth reported patient, without naming agents.

evidence.snippet: She continued to have multiple daily subclinical breakthrough seizures despite maximum doses of phenobarbital, levetiracetam, and lacosamide along with initiation of a ketogenic diet (maximum beta-hydroxybutyrate achieved 2.04 mmol/L).
evidence.explanation: Names three of the agents used and records that the seizures were resistant to them at maximum dose, which is why no agent is presented as effective.

evidence.snippet: At 14-month follow-up, she was being treated with vigabatrin 500 mg q12, brivaracetam 30 mg q12, levetiracetam 400 mg q12, and phenobarbital 22.4 mg q12 via gastrostomy tube.
evidence.explanation: Names the two further agents, vigabatrin and brivaracetam, in the maintenance regimen.

treatments/3.description: Seizures have been treated with standard antiseizure medication in two reported patients. In the fifth patient the epilepsy was drug-resistant: breakthrough seizures continued on maximum doses of phenobarbital, levetiracetam and lacosamide, and the regimen at 14 months was vigabatrin, brivaracetam, levetiracetam and phenobarbital. No genotype-directed response rate has been reported, and no agent is recommended for this disease specifically.

evidence.snippet: She continued to have multiple daily subclinical breakthrough seizures despite maximum doses of phenobarbital, levetiracetam, and lacosamide along with initiation of a ketogenic diet (maximum beta-hydroxybutyrate achieved 2.04 mmol/L).
evidence.explanation: Records the ketogenic diet, the ketosis achieved, and that seizures persisted despite it.

treatments/4.description: A ketogenic diet was added to antiseizure medication in the fifth patient for drug-resistant epilepsy, reaching a maximum beta-hydroxybutyrate of 2.04 mmol/L. Breakthrough seizures continued on it, so it is recorded as attempted rather than as effective.

evidence.snippet: Third ventriculostomy and choroid plexus cauterization were undertaken for management of the hydrocephalus.
evidence.explanation: Names both procedures and their indication.

treatments/5.description: The hydrocephalus accompanying the Dandy-Walker anomaly in the fifth patient was managed neurosurgically. The NCIT term names the ventriculostomy; the choroid plexus cauterization performed with it has no NCIT clinical-action term and is recorded in the treatment name and description instead.

open_questions/0.rationale: The disagreement is real and is recorded rather than resolved, but it is worth stating precisely what it is. Reading the GenCC submissions, the split tracks how much of the literature each submission counted, not a disagreement about the same evidence: the two Strong submissions cite five and ten PMIDs including the 2016 reports, while the Supportive and Limited submissions each cite only the 2009 index report, and the Limited classification is dated 2015, before two of the five published families were reported. There is no ClinGen gene-disease validity curation. What would settle it is a formal ClinGen curation counting all five families and the four independently characterised alleles; this entry does not pre-empt that, and describes the relationship as reported rather than as definitive.

evidence.snippet: Consistent with this, obesity-associated single nucleotide polymorphisms are associated with expression of IRX3, but not FTO, in human brains.
evidence.explanation: The cleanest statement of the point: the obesity variants track IRX3 expression and not FTO expression. This is why an obesity citation cannot support a claim about FTO protein function.

evidence.snippet: The rs1421085 T-to-C single-nucleotide variant disrupts a conserved motif for the ARID5B repressor, which leads to derepression of a potent preadipocyte enhancer and a doubling of IRX3 and IRX5 expression during early adipocyte differentiation.
evidence.explanation: The mechanism worked out to the level of a single base and a repressor motif, confirming the obesity association operates through IRX3 and IRX5 rather than through FTO.

open_questions/1.rationale: Recorded because it is the retrieval trap this entry exists inside, and because the next curator will hit it. Searching FTO returns overwhelmingly the common intron-1 variants associated with body mass index. Those variants do not act on FTO protein function: the obesity-associated interval is a long-range regulatory landscape for the neighbouring homeobox genes IRX3 and IRX5, and the obesity-associated SNPs correlate with IRX3 expression rather than FTO expression in human brain. So an obesity-locus citation is not weak evidence for this disease; it is evidence about a regulatory element that happens to sit inside this gene. This is marked RESOLVED rather than OPEN because the question has an answer, and the answer is what governed which citations this entry accepts.

evidence.snippet: We find that recombinant murine Fto catalyzes the Fe(II)- and 2OG-dependent demethylation of 3-methylthymine in single-stranded DNA, with concomitant production of succinate, formaldehyde, and carbon dioxide.
evidence.explanation: The characterisation the 2009 index report's assay followed. Cited to date the state of knowledge, not as evidence about the disease.

evidence.snippet: We report here that fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) has efficient oxidative demethylation activity targeting the abundant N6-methyladenosine (m(6)A) residues in RNA in vitro.
evidence.explanation: The later substrate identification that the 2023 report's assay follows. Cited to date the shift in what is measured, not as evidence about the disease.

open_questions/2.rationale: The assay used has changed with the field rather than with the disease. The 2009 index report assayed 3-methylthymidine turnover in single-stranded DNA, following the 2007 characterisation of FTO, and predates the 2011 identification of FTO as the first mRNA m6A demethylase. The 2023 report assayed m6A. No study has tested which activity the developmental phenotype requires, and the alleles do not separate the question because they reduce both. This matters for whether the disease belongs with the epitranscriptomic disorders or with the nucleic-acid repair dioxygenases, which are different mechanistic neighbourhoods, and it is the reason no module conformance is declared on the enzymatic node.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that the loss of Fto in mice leads to postnatal growth retardation and a significant reduction in adipose tissue and lean body mass.
evidence.explanation: The reported null-mouse phenotype, which contains growth retardation and not malformation. This is the observation the mismatch rests on.

evidence.snippet: Congruently, Fto knockout mice display aberrant tissue specific cilia.
evidence.explanation: The reason the mouse cannot simply be called uninformative: the same knockout does show a ciliary abnormality, which is the mechanism proposed for the malformations. What is absent is the malformation itself, or a report of anyone having looked.

open_questions/3.rationale: The mouse reproduces the growth arm of the human phenotype and not the malformation arm, which is the arm this entry's central pathophysiology node asserts. The zebrafish, by contrast, does reproduce the malformation arm - growth retardation, craniofacial dysmorphism, microcephaly and neural crest defects - so the mismatch is not simply "no model shows malformations". It is that the two models disagree with each other, and the mouse disagrees with itself: the same Fto knockouts that show no reported CNS or cardiovascular malformation do show tissue-specific ciliary abnormality. Three readings are open and nobody has separated them. The developmental requirement for FTO may differ across species; the mouse comparison may be wrong in kind, since every human patient carries a missense allele with residual protein and no human null has ever been reported; or mouse malformations may simply not have been looked for, since the null was made and phenotyped to study energy homeostasis. The absence of any reported human null allele is itself notable and could mean complete FTO loss is not viable in humans. No knock-in animal carrying a patient missense allele has been reported in any species.

evidence.snippet: Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA or antigens is reported in some organs, yet the mechanism by which they do so and how they may be associated with pathogenic immune responses is unclear.
evidence.explanation: Links Long COVID to persistence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA or antigen in tissues and resulting immune responses.

evidence.snippet: We detect severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 spike predominantly in PASC patients up to 12 months after diagnosis.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates persistent circulating SARS-CoV-2 spike protein as a biomarker for PASC up to 12 months post-diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: we detected persistent SARS-CoV-2 RNA in multiple anatomic sites, including throughout the brain, as late as 230 days following symptom onset in one case.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that SARS-CoV-2 RNA can persist in human tissue, including brain, for months. The cohort is 44 people who died with COVID-19, predominantly after severe acute disease, so it demonstrates that tissue persistence is biologically possible rather than that a reservoir sustains symptoms in living Long COVID patients.

evidence.snippet: we established the presence of the residual virus in the appendix, skin, and breast tissues of 2 patients who exhibited LC symptoms 163 and 426 days after symptom onset.
evidence.explanation: The rare case where residual antigen and RNA were found in tissue from living, symptomatic Long COVID patients rather than at autopsy. It is a two-patient series and detects nucleocapsid protein and RNA only, so it does not establish replication-competent virus or that the residual antigen causes the symptoms.

steps/0.description: SARS-CoV-2 viral reservoirs may persist in tissues including gut, brain, and other organs for months after acute infection. The gastrointestinal tract has emerged as a particularly significant reservoir site, with viral RNA detected in approximately 30% of intestinal specimens from Long COVID patients.

evidence.snippet: The result, as is strongly manifested in platelet-poor plasma (PPP) of individuals with Long COVID, is extensive fibrin amyloid microclots that can persist, can entrap other proteins, and that may lead to the production of various autoantibodies.
evidence.explanation: Documents the presence and persistence of amyloid fibrin microclots in Long COVID patients.

evidence.snippet: the ability of these fibrin amyloid microclots (fibrinaloids) to block up capillaries, and thus to limit the passage of red blood cells and hence O2 exchange, can actually underpin the majority of these symptoms
evidence.explanation: Explains how microclots may cause Long COVID symptoms through impaired oxygen delivery.

evidence.snippet: The particles are amyloid and include fibrin(ogen); amyloid is not a part of a thrombus which is a mix of fibrin mesh and platelets.
evidence.explanation: Directly contests the "microclot" framing this node's name and description use. A Cochrane appraisal of the underlying laboratory studies concludes the observed structures are amyloid fibrin(ogen) particles and have not been shown to be thrombi, so intravascular clotting and capillary obstruction should be read as the hypothesis under test rather than as established properties of the particles.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that fibrin binds to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, forming proinflammatory blood clots that drive systemic thromboinflammation and neuropathology in COVID-19.
evidence.explanation: Independent mechanistic support for abnormal spike-fibrin biology, showing that fibrin is required for oxidative stress, macrophage activation and neuroinflammation after infection and that blocking its inflammatory domain is protective. It establishes a fibrin-driven inflammatory route rather than the mechanical perfusion-blockade route this node asserts, and it does not demonstrate persistent circulating amyloid particles or capillary occlusion in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: This reduction in peak VO2 was associated with impaired systemic oxygen extraction
evidence.explanation: Invasive cardiopulmonary exercise testing localizes post-COVID exertional intolerance to a peripheral oxygen-extraction limit with preserved cardiac index, which is the physiological deficit this node's perfusion mechanism predicts. Impaired extraction is not specific to microclots - mitochondrial, autonomic and deconditioning models predict it equally - and the study neither measured particles nor imaged capillary flow.

steps/1.description: Persistent endothelial damage and formation of amyloid-like fibrin microclots impair microcirculation. These anomalous fibrin deposits resist normal fibrinolysis and can block capillaries, limiting oxygen delivery to tissues and potentially explaining the diverse symptomatology of Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: we identify a lung-joint axis in which elevated endothelin-1 (ET-1) in alveolar type Ⅱ cells (AT2) disrupts iron homeostasis and contributes to cartilage and growth plate injury after SARS-CoV-2 infection
evidence.explanation: Locates the ET-1 elevation in AT2 cells as the proximal step of the lung-joint axis.

steps/2.description: Endothelin-1 is elevated in alveolar type II cells after SARS-CoV-2 infection, the proximal step of a lung-joint axis linking respiratory infection to skeletal injury. Reported in COVID-19 patient lung tissue by scRNA sequencing and histopathology.

evidence.snippet: the possible persistence of gut dysbiosis after disease resolution may be linked to long-COVID syndrome and particularly to its neurological manifestations
evidence.explanation: Links persistent gut dysbiosis to Long COVID syndrome and neurological symptoms.

evidence.snippet: Preliminary data seem to suggest that gut and airway dysbiosis might play a role in COVID-19 and in long-COVID neurological symptoms.
evidence.explanation: Supports the role of gut-brain axis disruption in Long COVID neurological manifestations.

evidence.snippet: Gut microbiota composition at admission was associated with occurrence of PACS.
evidence.explanation: Replaces review-level support with a primary prospective cohort - 106 patients serially sampled to 6 months against 68 controls, in which patients without PACS recovered a control-like microbiome while those with PACS did not. The design is observational, so acute severity, treatment and diet remain plausible confounders and the association falls short of independent prediction or causation.

evidence.snippet: Gut microbiome of patients with PACS were characterised by higher levels of Ruminococcus gnavus, Bacteroides vulgatus and lower levels of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii.
evidence.explanation: Gives the taxon-level content of the dysbiosis this node asserts, including depletion of the butyrate producer Faecalibacterium prausnitzii. Taxon-level results differ across cohorts by geography, diet, medication and sequencing method, so this is one cohort's signature rather than a validated diagnostic signature for Long COVID.

steps/3.description: Persistent gut microbiota dysbiosis has been observed in Long COVID patients, with alterations in microbial composition linked to immune inflammation and neurological manifestations through gut-lung and gut-brain axis disruption.

evidence.snippet: Several studies show preexisting and/or de novo production of autoantibodies after infection with SARS-CoV-2, but the persistence of these antibodies and their role in causing long COVID is debated.
evidence.explanation: Reviews evidence for autoantibody production in Long COVID pathogenesis.

evidence.snippet: Serology revealed an elevation in a variety of autoantibodies in LC.
evidence.explanation: Directly demonstrates elevated autoantibodies in Long COVID patients with ME/CFS.

evidence.snippet: Meta-analysis revealed a significantly higher number of seropositive ACE2 AAbs in COVID-19 patients
evidence.explanation: Pooled evidence that at least one receptor-directed autoantibody specificity (anti-ACE2) is genuinely enriched after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Scope is narrower than the headline suggests - only nine of the 68 reviewed studies entered the meta-analysis, and the parallel angiotensin-II autoantibody comparison was null - so this bounds rather than establishes a broad pathogenic autoantibody signature.

evidence.snippet: Differences between individuals who did or did not later develop PASC were, in comparison, more limited, but included significant differences in autoantibodies and in epigenetic and transcriptional signatures in double-negative 1 B cells, in particular.
evidence.explanation: Prospective multi-omic profiling of 341 patients at acute presentation ties incident PASC to autoantibody differences and to double-negative 1 B cells, the extrafollicular subset implicated in this node's B-cell dysregulation mechanism. The paper is explicit that these early signals were modest relative to severity-driven differences.

steps/4.description: SARS-CoV-2 infection can trigger preexisting and de novo production of autoantibodies through B-cell dysregulation, molecular mimicry, and bystander activation. These autoantibodies may contribute to the persistence and diversity of Long COVID symptoms.

evidence.snippet: Through scRNA sequencing and histopathological analysis of COVID-19 patients' and infected hamsters' lung and joint tissues, elevated ET-1 is linked to dysregulated iron homeostasis and iron accumulation
evidence.explanation: Graded HUMAN_CLINICAL for the COVID-19 patient lung and joint tissue in this analysis; the same sentence also reports the parallel hamster finding, and the abstract does not separate the two, so the human component is what this item is cited for.

steps/5.description: Disrupted iron homeostasis with iron accumulation in lung and joint tissue downstream of elevated lung epithelial ET-1. Observed in COVID-19 patient and infected hamster tissue.

evidence.snippet: the FDA-approved endothelin receptor antagonist, macitentan, protected infected hamsters from joint damage by reducing iron overload-associated chondrocyte dropout in both acute and subacute phase of infection in vivo
evidence.explanation: Blocking the upstream ET-1 receptor prevents chondrocyte dropout and joint damage in infected hamsters, establishing this node as the skeletal endpoint of the axis. INDIRECT because the measurement is a therapeutic rescue in a non-human model.

steps/6.description: Iron overload-associated chondrocyte dropout with cartilage and growth plate injury, the skeletal endpoint of the lung-joint axis.

evidence.snippet: Viral infection and type I interferon-driven inflammation reduce serotonin through three mechanisms: diminished intestinal absorption of the serotonin precursor tryptophan; platelet hyperactivation and thrombocytopenia, which impacts serotonin storage; and enhanced MAO-mediated serotonin turnover.
evidence.explanation: Describes the three mechanistic drivers of serotonin loss in Long COVID; the mechanistic pathway is demonstrated in mouse models in this paper.

steps/7.description: Long COVID features reduced peripheral serotonin driven by diminished intestinal tryptophan absorption, platelet hyperactivation that depletes stored serotonin, and enhanced monoamine oxidase-mediated serotonin turnover.

evidence.snippet: Peripheral serotonin reduction, in turn, impedes the activity of the vagus nerve and thereby impairs hippocampal responses and memory.
evidence.explanation: Connects serotonin loss to vagal signaling deficits and hippocampal dysfunction in mouse models.

steps/8.description: Peripheral serotonin depletion weakens vagus nerve activity, leading to impaired hippocampal responses and memory formation that contribute to cognitive symptoms in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: It encompasses a plethora of debilitating symptoms (including breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations and orthostatic intolerance)
evidence.explanation: Lists breathlessness (dyspnea) among the debilitating symptoms of Long COVID.

steps/9.description: Shortness of breath and breathing difficulties persisting after acute infection.

evidence.snippet: They develop persistent fatigue, cognitive problems, headaches, disrupted sleep
evidence.explanation: Documents disrupted sleep as a symptom that interferes with function.

steps/10.description: Insomnia, unrefreshing sleep, or altered sleep patterns.

evidence.snippet: Across at least 10 cohorts, authors reported 31 unique clinical features corresponding to HPO terms; the most commonly reported feature was Fatigue (median 45.1%)
evidence.explanation: Insomnia was among the 31 most commonly reported clinical features across Long COVID cohorts.

steps/11.description: Difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.

evidence.snippet: the role(s) that viral persistence or reactivation of viruses may play in PASC.
evidence.explanation: RECOVER review-level evidence supports modeling viral reactivation as a Long COVID mechanism distinct from SARS-CoV-2 reservoir persistence.

evidence.snippet: Serological evidence suggesting recent EBV reactivation (early antigen-diffuse IgG positivity) was most strongly associated with fatigue (OR = 2.12).
evidence.explanation: Provides human post-acute cohort evidence linking EBV reactivation serology to a Long COVID symptom domain.

evidence.snippet: emerging evidence suggests that the reactivation of latent viral infections, such as Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and varicella-zoster virus, may significantly contribute to the complexity of LC.
evidence.explanation: Supports EBV/CMV/VZV latent-virus reactivation as a plausible but incompletely stratified contributor to Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: We resolved four PASC-anticipating risk factors at the time of initial COVID-19 diagnosis: type 2 diabetes, SARS-CoV-2 RNAemia, Epstein-Barr virus viremia, and specific auto-antibodies.
evidence.explanation: Multi-omic longitudinal cohort identifies EBV viremia at acute COVID-19 as one of four early PASC-anticipating factors.

evidence.snippet: we found that 66.7% (20/30) of long COVID subjects versus 10% (2/20) of control subjects in our primary study group were positive for EBV reactivation based on positive titers for EBV early antigen-diffuse (EA-D) IgG or EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates a markedly higher EBV reactivation rate (by EA-D IgG / VCA IgM serology) in Long COVID patients versus controls.

evidence.snippet: higher antibody responses directed against non-SARS-CoV-2 viral pathogens were observed among individuals with long COVID, particularly Epstein-Barr virus.
evidence.explanation: Independent immune-profiling cohort confirms heightened anti-EBV antibody responses in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: High EBV antibody levels were significantly associated with a more than fourfold increased odds of experiencing fatigue during acute COVID-19 disease and during follow-up.
evidence.explanation: A further independent German follow-up cohort (n=62 through 20 months) reproduces the EBV-fatigue association and extends it to CMV with concentration problems and taste loss. The authors state explicitly that whether these antibody levels indicate reactivation remains to be elucidated, so this is a serological association and not a demonstration of productive viral reactivation.

steps/12.description: SARS-CoV-2-associated immune dysregulation may permit reactivation of latent herpesviruses. EBV has the strongest cohort-level support in Long COVID; CMV and VZV remain plausible latent-virus contributors that require biomarker-stratified confirmation.

evidence.snippet: LC individuals exhibited systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation. This was evidenced by global differences in T cell subset distribution implying ongoing immune responses, as well as by sex-specific perturbations in cytolytic subsets.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates persistent systemic inflammation and altered immune signaling in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: Marked differences were noted in circulating myeloid and lymphocyte populations relative to the matched controls, as well as evidence of exaggerated humoral responses directed against SARS-CoV-2 among participants with long COVID.
evidence.explanation: Immune profiling shows broad myeloid/lymphocyte shifts and heightened humoral responses in Long COVID.

steps/13.description: Long COVID patients show ongoing systemic inflammation with altered T cell subset distributions and cytokine perturbations, indicating chronic immune activation and dysregulated signaling.

evidence.snippet: LC individuals displayed increased frequencies of CD4+ T cells poised to migrate to inflamed tissues and exhausted SARS-CoV-2-specific CD8+ T cells
evidence.explanation: Documents tissue-trafficking CD4+ cells and exhausted virus-specific CD8+ cells in Long COVID.

steps/14.description: SARS-CoV-2-specific CD8+ T cells exhibit exhaustion phenotypes while CD4+ T cells are poised to migrate to inflamed tissues, reflecting sustained antigen exposure and chronic activation in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: Previous studies have suggested that mast cell activation (MCA) may play a role in the pathophysiology of long-COVID, including in the mechanisms of its cardiovascular manifestations.
evidence.explanation: Implicates mast cell activation in Long COVID pathophysiology.

evidence.snippet: Long-COVID symptoms disappeared completely in 29% of treated patients. There was a significant improvement in each of the considered symptoms (improved or disappeared) in all treated patients
evidence.explanation: Treatment response to antihistamines supports the role of mast cell activation in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: PCS+ individuals exhibited a distinct immune profile characterized by increased mast cell activity, and elevated zonulin levels, indicating compromised gut barrier function alongside with elevated SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein expression in the TI.
evidence.explanation: Direct human tissue evidence of increased mast cell activity in post-COVID syndrome, from terminal-ileum biopsies 15-22 months after infection in 43 convalescent patients. Note this is the gut compartment - it does not close the separate gap that no study has demonstrated mast-cell activation in Long COVID brain or CSF.

steps/15.description: Mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) has been implicated in Long COVID pathophysiology. Mast cell degranulation releases pro-inflammatory mediators including histamine, contributing to fatigue, brain fog, cardiovascular symptoms, and gastrointestinal disturbances.

evidence.snippet: Activation of microglia in response to an immune system challenge can lead to a significant impact on cognitive processes, such as learning, memory and emotional regulation.
evidence.explanation: Documents microglial activation and its impact on cognitive processes in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: Inflammatory cytokines have been found to play a significant role in reductions in LTP and LTD, a reduction in neurogenesis, and in dendritic sprouting.
evidence.explanation: Explains how inflammatory cytokines impair neural function in Long COVID brain fog.

evidence.snippet: our pilot study of CSF markers indicates that persistent post-COVID-19 headache is not a sign of underlying neuronal damage or glial activation.
evidence.explanation: The only direct CSF measurement cited in this entry, and it is negative - neurofilament light chain, UCH-L1, tau and GFAP were not elevated in post-COVID persistent headache. Two limits on how far it cuts against this node - it is a pilot study restricted to a headache phenotype, and it assays neuronal and astrocytic injury markers rather than microglial activation or mast-cell mediators such as tryptase and histamine, so it does not test the mast-cell arm of the pathway.

steps/16.description: Neuroinflammation in Long COVID involves microglial activation, blood-brain barrier disruption, and inflammatory cytokine penetration into the brain parenchyma. This contributes to cognitive dysfunction, memory impairment, and other neurological symptoms.

evidence.snippet: Dopaminergic neurons are vulnerable to injury from gliosis and have high density of ACE2 receptors, but the integrity of dopaminergic neurons has not been investigated in long COVID.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the rationale for dopaminergic vulnerability in Long COVID (gliosis susceptibility and high ACE2 density on dopamine neurons) that the VMAT2 PET study set out to test.

evidence.snippet: Findings of reduced VMAT2 binding may reflect reduced dopaminergic terminal integrity in long COVID.
evidence.explanation: The primary study interprets reduced striatal VMAT2 binding as reduced dopaminergic terminal integrity.

evidence.snippet: midbrain dopamine (DA) neurons derived from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) are selectively susceptible and permissive to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. SARS-CoV-2 infection of DA neurons triggers an inflammatory and cellular senescence response.
evidence.explanation: hPSC-derived dopamine neurons are selectively susceptible to SARS-CoV-2 and mount inflammatory/senescence responses, a candidate cellular mechanism for dopaminergic terminal dysfunction.

steps/17.description: A neuropsychiatric endotype of Long COVID is marked by reduced integrity of presynaptic dopaminergic terminals in the striatum. (+)[11C]DTBZ PET, an index of vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2) binding and dopamine-releasing neuron density, is significantly lower in the ventral striatum, dorsal putamen, and dorsal caudate of adults with Long COVID, and lower regional binding tracks with apathy, motor slowing, and memory decline. Experimentally, midbrain dopamine neurons are selectively susceptible to SARS-CoV-2 and respond with inflammatory and cellular-senescence programs, a candidate upstream driver. Reduced VMAT2 binding need not imply irreversible neuronal loss; it may reflect altered vesicular storage, regulatory transporter changes, or adaptive presynaptic remodeling, so this node is modeled as dopaminergic terminal dysfunction rather than frank nigrostriatal neurodegeneration.

evidence.snippet: The vagus nerve inflammatory reflex is an important, well-characterized mechanism for the reflexive suppression of cytokine storm, and its experimental or clinical impairment facilitates the onset and progression of hyperinflammation.
evidence.explanation: Indirect support only. The paper documents impaired vagal anti-inflammatory reflexes driving systemic hyperinflammation; it does not address the BBB or tight junctions directly. Cited as an upstream systemic-inflammation contributor to BBB dysfunction, not as direct BBB evidence.

evidence.snippet: MC activation and degranulation destroyed the tight junction proteins in brain microvascular endothelial cells and induced the activation and proliferation of microglia.
evidence.explanation: Directly demonstrates SARS-CoV-2-triggered mast cell destruction of BBB tight junction proteins in brain microvascular endothelial cells in vitro.

steps/18.description: Long COVID is associated with increased blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability resulting from endothelial dysfunction and tight junction disruption. Increased BBB permeability permits systemic inflammatory cytokines and viral antigens to access the brain parenchyma, driving neuroinflammation and cognitive symptoms.

evidence.snippet: we posit that this condition may be related to a virus- or immune-mediated disruption of the autonomic nervous system resulting in orthostatic intolerance syndromes.
evidence.explanation: Proposes autonomic nervous system disruption as a key mechanism in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: 'Post-acute COVID' (known colloquially as 'long COVID') is emerging as a prevalent syndrome. It encompasses a plethora of debilitating symptoms (including breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations and orthostatic intolerance)
evidence.explanation: Documents the prevalence of autonomic symptoms in Long COVID.

steps/19.description: Dysautonomia, particularly postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), develops in many Long COVID patients. This may be related to virus- or immune-mediated disruption of the autonomic nervous system resulting in orthostatic intolerance syndromes.

evidence.snippet: Emerging evidence has pointed to mitochondrial dysfunction as a potential underpinning mechanism contributing to the persistence and diversity of long COVID symptoms.
evidence.explanation: Links mitochondrial dysfunction and reduced energy production to persistent Long COVID symptoms.

steps/20.description: Long COVID is associated with reduced mitochondrial ATP production and impaired oxidative phosphorylation, contributing to fatigue, cognitive disturbances, and exercise intolerance.

evidence.snippet: This review aims to synthesize current findings related to mitochondrial dysfunction in long COVID, exploring its implications for cellular energy deficits, oxidative stress, immune dysregulation, metabolic disturbances, and endothelial dysfunction.
evidence.explanation: Describes oxidative stress and metabolic disturbances resulting from mitochondrial dysfunction in Long COVID.

steps/21.description: Mitochondrial impairment drives a shift toward glycolysis with associated oxidative stress and metabolic disturbances, further exacerbating systemic symptoms in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: They develop persistent fatigue, cognitive problems, headaches, disrupted sleep, myalgias and arthralgias, post-exertional malaise, orthostatic intolerance and other symptoms that greatly interfere with their ability to function
evidence.explanation: Documents fatigue as a prominent symptom that interferes with function in Long COVID.

steps/22.description: Persistent, debilitating fatigue that is not relieved by rest.

evidence.snippet: They develop persistent fatigue, cognitive problems, headaches, disrupted sleep
evidence.explanation: Documents cognitive problems as a core symptom of Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: Peripheral serotonin reduction, in turn, impedes the activity of the vagus nerve and thereby impairs hippocampal responses and memory.
evidence.explanation: Provides mechanistic explanation for memory impairment via vagal-hippocampal pathway; mechanism demonstrated in mouse models.

steps/23.description: Brain fog, difficulty concentrating, memory problems, and reduced executive function. Often referred to as cognitive dysfunction.

evidence.explanation: Explicitly identifies post-exertional malaise as a core Long COVID symptom.

evidence.snippet: The illness (Long COVID) is similar to myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS)
evidence.explanation: Notes the similarity between Long COVID and ME/CFS, which share post-exertional malaise.

steps/24.description: Worsening of symptoms following physical or mental exertion, similar to myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome.

evidence.snippet: It encompasses a plethora of debilitating symptoms (including breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations and orthostatic intolerance)
evidence.explanation: Lists palpitations among the debilitating symptoms of Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: Cardiovascular manifestations of long-COVID include high heart rate, postural tachycardia, and palpitations.
evidence.explanation: Confirms palpitations as a cardiovascular manifestation of Long COVID.

steps/25.description: Awareness of heartbeat, often associated with POTS or general autonomic dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: Cardiovascular manifestations of long-COVID include high heart rate, postural tachycardia, and palpitations.
evidence.explanation: Documents high heart rate and postural tachycardia as Long COVID manifestations.

steps/26.description: Elevated heart rate, often associated with POTS or general autonomic dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: They develop persistent fatigue, cognitive problems, headaches, disrupted sleep
evidence.explanation: Lists headaches among the persistent symptoms following COVID-19.

evidence.snippet: The pooled prevalence of depression and anxiety among patients coping with Post COVID-19 syndrome was estimated to be 23% (95% CI: 20%-26%; I2 = 99.9%) based on data from 143 studies with 7,782,124 participants and 132 studies with 9,320,687 participants, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Meta-analysis establishes 23% prevalence of anxiety in Long COVID patients.

evidence.snippet: Patients suffering from post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) have a higher prevalence of anxiety and depression than the general population.
evidence.explanation: Documents higher prevalence of anxiety in PASC patients compared to general population.

steps/28.description: Increased anxiety levels and panic symptoms.

evidence.snippet: The pooled prevalence of depression and anxiety among patients coping with Post COVID-19 syndrome was estimated to be 23% (95% CI: 20%-26%; I2 = 99.9%) based on data from 143 studies with 7,782,124 participants
evidence.explanation: Meta-analysis establishes 23% prevalence of depression in Long COVID patients.

evidence.snippet: Overall, patients with PASC may have experienced a heavier burden of newly manifest anxiety and depression symptoms compared to patients seen in the GIM clinic.
evidence.explanation: Documents higher burden of newly manifest depression in Long COVID patients.

evidence.snippet: Loss of dopamine nerve terminals may be contributing to symptom correlates of apathy, motor slowing and memory decline
evidence.explanation: Establishes apathy as a neuropsychiatric symptom correlate of Long COVID linked to loss of striatal dopamine nerve terminals.

steps/30.description: Reduced motivation and goal-directed behavior. In a VMAT2 PET study, apathy was a measured neuropsychiatric outcome in adults with Long COVID and correlated with lower ventral striatal dopaminergic terminal binding, linking it to the striatal dopaminergic endotype.

evidence.snippet: They develop persistent fatigue, cognitive problems, headaches, disrupted sleep, myalgias and arthralgias
evidence.explanation: Lists myalgias as a persistent symptom of Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: They develop persistent fatigue, cognitive problems, headaches, disrupted sleep, myalgias and arthralgias

evidence.snippet: They develop persistent fatigue, cognitive problems, headaches, disrupted sleep, myalgias and arthralgias, post-exertional malaise, orthostatic intolerance

evidence.snippet: It encompasses a plethora of debilitating symptoms (including breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations and orthostatic intolerance)

steps/33.description: Excessive heart rate increase upon standing, characteristic of POTS.

evidence.snippet: curated 59 relevant manuscripts that described clinical manifestations in 81 cohorts three weeks or more following acute COVID-19, and mapped 287 unique clinical findings to HPO terms
evidence.explanation: Gastrointestinal symptoms including diarrhea were among the clinical manifestations mapped in Long COVID.

steps/34.description: Loose or watery bowel movements persisting after acute infection.

evidence.snippet: the most commonly reported feature was Fatigue (median 45.1%) and the least commonly reported was Nausea (median 3.9%)
evidence.explanation: Nausea was reported across multiple Long COVID cohorts with median prevalence of 3.9%.

steps/35.description: Sensation of unease in the stomach with urge to vomit.

evidence.snippet: Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA or antigens is reported in some organs, yet the mechanism by which they do so and how they may be associated with pathogenic immune responses is unclear.
evidence.explanation: Persistent tissue viral RNA/antigen supports continued immune stimulation in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: Despite extensive distribution of SARS-CoV-2 RNA throughout the body, we observed little evidence of inflammation or direct viral cytopathology outside the respiratory tract.
evidence.explanation: In the same autopsy series that established widespread RNA persistence, persistence was decoupled from tissue inflammation outside the airway. This argues that residual antigen is not by itself sufficient to drive the extrapulmonary immune activation this edge asserts.

edges/0.description: Persistent viral antigens drive chronic immune activation and cytokine perturbations.

evidence.snippet: Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA or antigens is reported in some organs, yet the mechanism by which they do so and how they may be associated with pathogenic immune responses is unclear.

edges/1.description: Sustained antigen exposure from viral reservoirs leads to CD8+ T cell exhaustion and CD4+ tissue trafficking.

evidence.snippet: Viral infection and type I interferon-driven inflammation reduce serotonin through three mechanisms: diminished intestinal absorption of the serotonin precursor tryptophan; platelet hyperactivation and thrombocytopenia, which impacts serotonin storage; and enhanced MAO-mediated serotonin turnover.

edges/2.description: Viral persistence and type I interferon-driven inflammation reduce serotonin through diminished tryptophan absorption, platelet hyperactivation, and enhanced MAO turnover.

evidence.snippet: COVID-19 infection could lead to exaggeration of existing undiagnosed mast cell activation syndrome, or could activate normal mast cells owing to the persistence of viral particles.

edges/3.description: Persistent viral antigens trigger mast cell degranulation and release of pro-inflammatory mediators.

evidence.snippet: These latent viruses can be reactivated by SARS-CoV-2, contributing to a chronic inflammatory state that prolongs symptomatology.
evidence.explanation: Supports latent-virus reactivation as an amplifier of chronic inflammatory states in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: These findings suggest that many long COVID symptoms may not be a direct result of the SARS-CoV-2 virus but may be the result of COVID-19 inflammation-induced EBV reactivation.
evidence.explanation: Links EBV reactivation to inflammation-driven Long COVID symptomatology.
