It measures particle burden and associated endothelial and neutrophil markers only, and proposes intravascular NETosis rather than capillary occlusion as the driver, so it does not establish the perfusion-limitation chain this hypothesis asserts.

hypotheses/2.description: Fibrin amyloid microclots impair capillary flow and oxygen exchange, driving fatigue, dyspnea, and energy deficits in a vascular-predominant subtype.

evidence.snippet: Peripheral serotonin reduction, in turn, impedes the activity of the vagus nerve and thereby impairs hippocampal responses and memory.
evidence.explanation: Supports an emerging gut-immune-neuro axis in Long COVID; this mechanistic link (serotonin → vagus nerve → hippocampus) is demonstrated in mouse models in this paper.

hypotheses/3.description: Interferon-linked serotonin depletion impairs vagal signaling and hippocampal responses, contributing to cognitive and autonomic symptoms.

evidence.snippet: These findings reveal a cellular mechanism of SARS-CoV-2-induced neuroinflammation.
evidence.explanation: Provides mechanistic cellular support for mast-cell-associated neuroinflammatory pathways.

hypotheses/4.description: Mast-cell activation may compromise BBB integrity and promote neuroinflammation, amplifying cognitive and neuropsychiatric manifestations.

evidence.snippet: Several studies show preexisting and/or de novo production of autoantibodies after infection with SARS-CoV-2, but the persistence of these antibodies and their role in causing long COVID is debated.
evidence.explanation: Supports autoimmunity as an emerging mechanistic hypothesis for Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: COVID-19 induces a marked though transient AAA1 response, independently predicting one-year persistence of respiratory symptoms.
evidence.explanation: Longitudinal serology in 193 hospital employees shows that an infection-induced autoantibody independently predicts one symptom domain at 12 months, supporting an autoantibody contribution to persistence. It remains a prediction, not a demonstration that the antibody caused the symptoms.

evidence.snippet: AAA1 seropositivity was 93% at one month and declined to 15% at 12 months after COVID-19.
evidence.explanation: Substantiates the persistence caveat in the notes above - this de novo autoantibody response largely resolves within a year, arguing against sustained autoantibody presence as the ongoing driver of established Long COVID.

hypotheses/5.description: SARS-CoV-2 triggers de novo autoantibody production through B-cell dysregulation, molecular mimicry, and bystander activation, contributing to multisystem symptoms and immune-mediated tissue damage in Long COVID.

evidence.snippet: the possible persistence of gut dysbiosis after disease resolution may be linked to long-COVID syndrome and particularly to its neurological manifestations
evidence.explanation: Supports gut dysbiosis as a contributing mechanism to Long COVID neurological symptoms.

evidence.snippet: At 6 months, significantly higher proportions of the SIM01 group had alleviation of fatigue
evidence.explanation: Cites the SIM01 trial named in the notes above - 463 participants randomized, double-blind and placebo-controlled, with alleviation of fatigue, memory loss, concentration difficulty, gastrointestinal upset and general unwellness. It is the only interventional support this hypothesis has. It is single-centre with declared inventor, equity and licensing interests, uses self-reported outcomes, and includes no mediation analysis, so it does not establish that correcting baseline dysbiosis is what produced the benefit.

evidence.snippet: we show that intestinal SARS-CoV-2 reservoirs disrupt very-long-chain fatty acid (VLCFA) metabolism, suppressing activation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling and reducing peroxisome abundance.
evidence.explanation: Cites the directional challenge described in the notes above. Combining patient data with transgenic animal models, dysbiosis appears as an output of intestinal viral reservoirs and failed epithelial regeneration, not as an independent upstream driver. It refutes the seed framing only in the gastrointestinal compartment, and a feedback loop between reservoir, barrier failure and dysbiosis remains compatible with both directions.

hypotheses/6.description: Persistent gut microbiota dysbiosis following SARS-CoV-2 infection disrupts gut-lung and gut-brain axis homeostasis, contributing to systemic immune dysregulation and neurological manifestations.

evidence.snippet: Loss of dopamine nerve terminals may be contributing to symptom correlates of apathy, motor slowing and memory decline suggesting improved function of dopaminergic synapses as a new therapeutic direction to treat long COVID.
evidence.explanation: Primary VMAT2 PET study links reduced striatal dopaminergic terminal integrity to the apathy/motor-slowing/memory-decline neuropsychiatric endotype and motivates a dopaminergic therapeutic direction.

evidence.snippet: SARS-CoV-2 infection of DA neurons triggers an inflammatory and cellular senescence response.
evidence.explanation: Provides the experimental mechanistic basis (dopamine-neuron infection triggering inflammation and senescence) underpinning the endotype.

hypotheses/7.description: A subset of Long COVID presents a measurable dopaminergic neuropsychiatric endotype: reduced striatal binding of vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2), an index of presynaptic dopaminergic terminal integrity, that tracks with apathy, psychomotor (motor) slowing, and memory decline. SARS-CoV-2 susceptibility of midbrain dopamine neurons, with inflammatory and senescence-like responses, provides a candidate upstream mechanism linking viral exposure to persistent dopaminergic dysfunction.

open_questions/0.rationale: The primary evidence is a single-center case-control (+)[11C]DTBZ PET study (24 vs 24, extended to 43 controls). Reduced VMAT2 binding is a robust marker of presynaptic monoaminergic terminal integrity but does not by itself distinguish reversible functional downregulation from neuronal loss. Resolving reversibility and disease-specificity determines whether the dopaminergic endotype is a treatment-responsive target (e.g., dopaminergic augmentation) versus a marker of established neurodegeneration, and whether it should ever conform to the parkinsonism_dopaminergic_degeneration module.

evidence.snippet: These findings reveal a cellular mechanism of SARS-CoV-2-induced neuroinflammation.
evidence.explanation: Supports a plausible mast-cell-mediated mechanism while leaving the necessity and causal ordering of mast-cell activation unresolved.

open_questions/1.rationale: The current evidence is mechanistically compelling but largely cellular and associative. A human neurovascular model with controlled mast-cell activation would test whether mast cells are sufficient and necessary for barrier dysfunction and microglial activation under SARS-CoV-2-relevant stimuli.

evidence.snippet: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir administered for 15 days did not significantly improve health outcomes in participants with long COVID compared with placebo-ritonavir at day 28.
evidence.explanation: The null antiviral trial result motivates the upstream/downstream distinction and the need for biomarker-stratified antiviral testing.

evidence.snippet: Here, we review the current state of knowledge regarding the biology and pathophysiology of long COVID, focusing on how the proposed mechanisms explain the physiology of the syndrome and how they provide a rationale for the implementation of a broad experimental medicine and clinical trials agenda.
evidence.explanation: Supports framing unresolved mechanistic ordering as a prerequisite for experimental-medicine trial design.

open_questions/2.rationale: The current graph places SARS-CoV-2 persistence upstream of immune activation, serotonin depletion, mast-cell activation, and other downstream nodes, but established Long COVID may include virus-independent immune, endothelial, autonomic, or autoimmune loops. The PAX LC nirmatrelvir-ritonavir trial did not significantly improve health outcomes at day 28, which does not refute viral persistence but makes the active-replicating-virus model insufficient as a single explanation for established disease. Resolving this hierarchy requires separating replication-competent virus, residual antigen/RNA, and self-sustaining downstream pathology in the same patients over time.

evidence.snippet: focusing on how the proposed mechanisms explain the physiology of the syndrome and how they provide a rationale for the implementation of a broad experimental medicine and clinical trials agenda.
evidence.explanation: Supports mechanism-level biology as the basis for therapeutic stratification and experimental trial design.

evidence.snippet: The relatively similar symptom profiles of individual PAISs, irrespective of the infectious agent, as well as the overlap of clinical features with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), suggest the potential involvement of a common etiopathogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Qualifies symptom-cluster interpretation by showing that similar symptoms can emerge across distinct infections.

evidence.snippet: Overall, these findings suggest differential effects of chronic viral coinfections on the likelihood of developing LC and association with distinct syndromic patterns.
evidence.explanation: Supports testing whether biomarker-defined mechanisms correspond to distinct Long COVID syndromic patterns.

open_questions/3.rationale: The entry currently maps hypotheses to broad symptom clusters, but the same symptom cluster could arise from different upstream mechanisms, and one mechanism can plausibly contribute to multiple clusters. This ambiguity weakens causal interpretation and trial design: anticoagulant therapy for a microclot-enriched subgroup, SSRI/serotonin-pathway intervention for a serotonin-depleted subgroup, antihistamine therapy for mast-cell-enriched patients, or antiviral/latent-virus approaches all require mechanism-level enrichment beyond symptom labels alone.

evidence.snippet: We discuss emerging relationships between long COVID and diabetes and the effect of vaccination on diabetes risk following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Finally, we identify critical knowledge gaps and outline priorities for ongoing and future studies needed to resolve remaining uncertainties.
evidence.explanation: Said et al. identify the Long COVID-to-diabetes link as a critical knowledge gap, noting that the mechanistic distinction between metabolic vs. autoimmune pathways to post-COVID diabetes remains unresolved and is essential for stratified therapeutics.

open_questions/4.rationale: A comprehensive post-pandemic review (Said et al. 2026, Diabetologia) of SARS-CoV-2 and diabetes identifies critical uncertainties about the mechanisms linking Long COVID to new-onset diabetes development post-COVID. Two mechanistic branches are unresolved: (1) whether persistent metabolic dysfunction and mitochondrial impairment in Long COVID drive insulin resistance in peripheral tissues (muscle, adipose) and Type 2-like hyperglycemia, or (2) whether Long COVID autoimmunity (beta-cell-targeting autoantibodies, persistent interferon dysregulation, EBV reactivation) contributes to Type 1-like beta-cell loss and insulin deficiency. The distinction is clinically consequential because metabolic insulin resistance suggests interventions targeting mitochondrial biogenesis, exercise capacity, and metabolic normalization, whereas autoimmunity suggests immune tolerance or regulatory T cell expansion. This entry models Long COVID pathophysiology; clarifying these causal edges informs post-COVID diabetes stratification and therapeutic design.

evidence.snippet: A convenience sample of patients undergoing an extended course of antiviral therapy was studied.
evidence.explanation: Documents the study design that is currently the strongest Long COVID evidence for anti-herpesvirus therapy, and thereby the gap. A convenience sample of 24 patients on off-label open-label treatment with patient-reported outcomes, no randomization, no placebo control, and declared inventor/company conflicts cannot establish efficacy or identify which of the two targeted viruses any benefit came from.

evidence.snippet: VGCV may have clinical benefit in a subset of CFS patients independent of placebo effect, possibly mediated by immunomodulation and/or antiviral effect.
evidence.explanation: The nearest controlled precedent, and it illustrates why the trial above is needed. This 30-patient randomized trial enrolled on elevated HHV-6/EBV titres yet could not separate an antiviral from an immunomodulatory mechanism, and viral IgG titres did not differ between arms - target engagement was never shown. It is also in ME/CFS, not Long COVID.

open_questions/5.rationale: The reactivation model rests almost entirely on serology. Antibody markers are elevated across six or more independent cohorts, but viremia is usually undetectable, and no study measures lytic gene expression or shows that the antibody signal tracks productive replication. That distinction only becomes testable through intervention: a therapy that measurably suppresses herpesvirus activity and then improves symptoms would separate driver from bystander, while a null result under confirmed target engagement would move the serology to a marker of immune history. The existing human evidence is an uncontrolled open-label case series in Long COVID and an indirect valganciclovir trial in ME/CFS, neither of which can settle this. The gap is the reason the hypothesis is held at EMERGING rather than upgraded.

evidence.snippet: Randomized controlled trials review We identified no trials meeting our inclusion criteria.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the interventional half of this gap as a systematic search result rather than an impression - a Cochrane review searching four databases plus two trial registries found no randomized trial of plasmapheresis for removing these particles in the post-COVID-19 condition. The review advises against the intervention outside a well-conducted trial.

evidence.snippet: This reduction in peak VO2 was associated with impaired systemic oxygen extraction
evidence.explanation: Supplies the physiological endpoint the imaging experiment must explain, and the reason the gap matters: the extraction deficit is real and measurable, but this study attributes it to a peripheral limit without identifying its cause, so it is compatible with the microclot model and with its mitochondrial and autonomic competitors alike.

open_questions/6.rationale: Each component of this model has support in isolation - particles are detectable in plasma, endothelial dysfunction is robust, and invasive exercise testing shows a peripheral oxygen-extraction limit - but the step that connects them has never been observed. No study has visualized a particle lodging in a capillary in a living patient, and none has shown that particle burden mediates the extraction deficit. The alternatives are live: the peripheral limit is equally predicted by mitochondrial, autonomic and deconditioning models, and the one independent Long COVID cohort to quantify the particles proposed intravascular NETosis rather than obstruction as the driver. A Cochrane appraisal found the particles in healthy and diabetic plasma as well, and found no eligible randomized trial of particle removal. Until either the occlusion step is imaged or an intervention that clears the particles changes symptoms, this hypothesis cannot move above ALTERNATIVE.

evidence.snippet: Here we identify dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP4; also known as CD26) as a functional receptor for hCoV-EMC.
evidence.explanation: Identifies DPP4 (CD26) as the functional host receptor for MERS-CoV (hCoV-EMC), the druggable host-factor entry step. Evidence source is IN_VITRO as this is a cell-based receptor-identification study.

evidence.snippet: Antibodies directed against DPP4 inhibited hCoV-EMC infection of primary human bronchial epithelial cells and Huh-7 cells.
evidence.explanation: Shows that blocking the host DPP4 receptor inhibits MERS-CoV infection of human bronchial epithelial cells, the host-directed antiviral proof of principle. Evidence source is IN_VITRO as this is a cell-culture experiment.

evidence.snippet: In humans it is primarily expressed on the epithelial cells in kidney, small intestine, liver and prostate, and on activated leukocytes
evidence.explanation: DPP4 tissue distribution — including renal, intestinal, and hepatic epithelium — is consistent with the extrapulmonary (renal and gastrointestinal) tropism of MERS beyond the respiratory tract. Evidence source is IN_VITRO as this receptor-characterization study reports the distribution of the host entry protein.

evidence.snippet: hCoV-EMC infection could not be blocked by the DPP4 inhibitors sitagliptin, vildagliptin, saxagliptin or P32/98
evidence.explanation: MERS-CoV entry depends on DPP4 as an attachment receptor rather than on its peptidase catalytic activity: clinically used gliptin DPP4 inhibitors did not block infection. Evidence source is IN_VITRO as this is a cell-culture inhibitor experiment.

steps/0.description: MERS-CoV enters host cells through its spike (S) glycoprotein, whose receptor-binding S1 domain engages the host cell-surface enzyme dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP4, also known as CD26); host serine proteases then prime the spike for membrane fusion. DPP4 is expressed on respiratory epithelium and pneumocytes, defining the tropism for the lower respiratory tract, and is also expressed on renal and intestinal epithelium and liver — a tissue distribution consistent with the extrapulmonary (notably renal and gastrointestinal) manifestations of severe MERS. Receptor engagement is independent of DPP4 enzymatic activity: clinically used gliptin DPP4 inhibitors do not block infection, so DPP4 serves as an attachment protein rather than through its peptidase catalysis. Because the receptor is a host protein, antibodies against DPP4 block infection — the host-directed-target logic shared with SARS-CoV-2/ACE2.

evidence.snippet: A previously unknown coronavirus was isolated from the sputum of a 60-year-old man who presented with acute pneumonia and subsequent renal failure with a fatal outcome in Saudi Arabia.
evidence.explanation: The index MERS case establishes the core severe phenotype — acute pneumonia with renal failure and a fatal outcome. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case report.

evidence.snippet: Disease caused by MERS-CoV presents with a wide range of clinical manifestations and is associated with substantial mortality in admitted patients who have medical comorbidities.
evidence.explanation: Descriptive cohort of 47 cases establishing the wide clinical spectrum and substantial mortality in comorbid patients. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

evidence.snippet: 28 patients died, a 60% case-fatality rate. The case-fatality rate rose with increasing age.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the high case-fatality of hospitalized MERS in the primary Saudi cohort and its rise with age, supporting the severe outcome and age-dependent mortality. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/1.description: MERS-CoV replication in the lower respiratory tract produces severe pneumonia that frequently progresses to acute respiratory distress syndrome and respiratory failure. Systemic and extrapulmonary involvement — notably acute kidney injury and gastrointestinal symptoms — is common, and the disease carries a high case-fatality rate concentrated in older adults with comorbidities.

evidence.snippet: A previously unknown coronavirus was isolated from the sputum of a 60-year-old man who presented with acute pneumonia and subsequent renal failure with a fatal outcome in Saudi Arabia.
evidence.explanation: The index case presented with acute pneumonia. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case report.

evidence.snippet: All patients had abnormal findings on chest radiography, ranging from subtle to extensive unilateral and bilateral abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Every patient in the 47-case cohort had abnormal chest radiography, reflecting the near-universal pulmonary involvement of symptomatic MERS. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/2.description: Severe viral pneumonia is the defining manifestation of symptomatic MERS.

evidence.snippet: Common symptoms at presentation were fever (46 [98%])
evidence.explanation: Fever was the most common presenting symptom in the 47-case series, present in 46 of 47 (98%), supporting a VERY_FREQUENT band. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/3.description: Fever is the most common presenting symptom of MERS.

evidence.explanation: Cough was present in 39 of 47 patients (83%) in the primary Saudi cohort, supporting a VERY_FREQUENT band. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/4.description: Cough is a common presenting symptom of MERS, reported in the majority of the 47-case Saudi series.

evidence.snippet: shortness of breath (34 [72%])
evidence.explanation: Shortness of breath (dyspnea) was present in 34 of 47 patients (72%) in the primary Saudi cohort, supporting a FREQUENT band. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/5.description: Shortness of breath is a frequent presenting symptom and reflects progression to severe lower respiratory disease.

evidence.snippet: A previously unknown coronavirus was isolated from the sputum of a 60-year-old man who presented with acute pneumonia and subsequent renal failure with a fatal outcome in Saudi Arabia.
evidence.explanation: The index case developed renal failure, the characteristic extrapulmonary manifestation. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case report.

steps/6.description: Renal failure is a characteristic extrapulmonary complication of severe MERS.

evidence.snippet: diarrhoea (12 [26%])
evidence.explanation: Diarrhoea was reported in 12 of 47 patients (26%) in the primary Saudi cohort, supporting an OCCASIONAL band. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/7.description: Gastrointestinal symptoms including diarrhea occur in a substantial minority of MERS cases.

evidence.snippet: vomiting (ten [21%])
evidence.explanation: Vomiting was reported in 10 of 47 patients (21%) in the primary Saudi cohort, supporting an OCCASIONAL band. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/8.description: Vomiting occurs as part of the gastrointestinal symptom complex in a minority of MERS cases.

evidence.snippet: myalgia (15 [32%])
evidence.explanation: Myalgia was reported in 15 of 47 patients (32%) in the primary Saudi cohort, supporting a FREQUENT band. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/9.description: Myalgia is a common systemic symptom at presentation in MERS.

evidence.snippet: lymphopenia (16 [34%])
evidence.explanation: Lymphopenia was present in 16 of 47 patients (34%) in the primary Saudi cohort, supporting a FREQUENT band. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/10.description: Lymphopenia is a characteristic laboratory feature of MERS, reflecting the lymphotropic and immunopathologic component of severe infection.

evidence.snippet: thrombocytopenia (17 [36%])
evidence.explanation: Thrombocytopenia was present in 17 of 47 patients (36%) in the primary Saudi cohort, supporting a FREQUENT band. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL as this is a clinical case series.

steps/11.description: Thrombocytopenia is a laboratory abnormality seen in a substantial minority of MERS cases.

edges/0.description: Productive infection of the lower respiratory epithelium drives severe pneumonia that can progress to ARDS and multiorgan involvement.

edges/1.description: MERS-CoV replication in the lower respiratory tract produces severe viral pneumonia.

edges/2.description: Severe infection drives a systemic febrile inflammatory response.

edges/3.description: Lower respiratory infection produces cough.

edges/4.description: Pneumonia and respiratory failure manifest clinically as dyspnea.

edges/5.description: Systemic and extrapulmonary spread includes acute renal involvement.

edges/6.description: Gastrointestinal involvement can produce diarrhea.

edges/7.description: Gastrointestinal involvement can produce vomiting.

edges/8.description: Systemic inflammation can manifest as myalgia.

edges/9.description: Severe MERS perturbs circulating lymphocyte counts.

edges/10.description: Severe MERS can lower platelet counts.

treatments/0.description: Management of MERS is primarily supportive, including supplemental oxygen and respiratory support (up to mechanical ventilation/ECMO for ARDS); no antiviral therapy is approved as standard of care, and management of severe disease is organ-supportive.

evidence.snippet: The 3D crystal structure of human VPS33A predicts that replacement of arginine 498 by tryptophan will de-stabilize VPS33A folding.
evidence.explanation: Structural basis for destabilisation of VPS33A by the founder p.Arg498Trp substitution.

evidence.snippet: We propose that the disease is due to diminished intracellular abundance of intact VPS33A.
evidence.explanation: States the proposed proximal disease mechanism: reduced abundance of intact VPS33A rather than an altered catalytic activity.

evidence.snippet: We showed decreased abundance of VPS33A in patient derived fibroblasts and provided evidence that the p.Arg200Pro mutation leads to destablization of the protein and proteasomal degradation.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the same destabilisation-and-proteasomal-degradation mechanism for the second, juvenile-associated VPS33A variant.

steps/1.description: Biallelic missense variants in VPS33A destabilise the folded protein and target it for proteasomal degradation, so the steady-state intracellular abundance of intact full-length VPS33A falls. The 3D crystal structure of human VPS33A predicts that replacement of arginine 498 by tryptophan de-stabilises folding; the same instability-plus-degradation mechanism is documented for the juvenile p.Arg200Pro variant. The functional consequence is hypomorphic loss of function through protein instability, not gain of function or dominant-negative activity, and mutant protein can be rescued by proteasome inhibition.

evidence.snippet: VPS33A is a core component of the class C core vacuole/endosome tethering (CORVET) and the homotypic fusion and protein sorting (HOPS) complexes, which have essential functions in the endocytic pathway.
evidence.explanation: Establishes VPS33A as a shared core subunit of both HOPS and CORVET, the structural reason a single-gene lesion depletes two tethering complexes.

evidence.snippet: We observed that the missense mutation reduced the abundance of full-length VPS33A and other components of the HOPS and CORVET complexes.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents secondary depletion of the other HOPS/CORVET components in cells carrying the mutant VPS33A.

evidence.snippet: A rare and fatal disease resembling mucopolysaccharidosis in infants, is caused by impaired intracellular endocytic trafficking due to deficiency of core components of the intracellular membrane-tethering protein complexes, HOPS, and CORVET.
evidence.explanation: Frames the disease itself as a deficiency of HOPS/CORVET core components causing impaired endocytic trafficking. Evidence source is OTHER because this is the paper's framing/background sentence rather than a report of its own patient or experimental data.

steps/2.description: VPS33A is a core component of the class C core vacuole/endosome tethering (CORVET) and the homotypic fusion and protein sorting (HOPS) complexes, which have essential functions in the endocytic pathway. Because VPS33A is shared by both complexes, its depletion is not isolated: patient cells show reduced abundance of the other HOPS and CORVET components as well, so both the early-endosome (CORVET) and late-endosome/lysosome (HOPS) tethering arms are simultaneously compromised.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that cultured fibroblasts from patients with this disorder have morphological changes: vacuolation with disordered endosomal/lysosomal compartments
evidence.explanation: Documents the disordered endosomal/lysosomal compartments and vacuolation in patient-derived cells.

evidence.snippet: indicated specific changes in cellular vacuoles, elevated levels of the EEA1 protein
evidence.explanation: Independent cell-biological confirmation of a disturbed endosomal compartment, with elevated EEA1 marking the early/late endosome fusion and sorting step.

evidence.snippet: Recent works demonstrated that low abundance of mutated VPS33A causes defective endosomal trafficking, resulting in poor delivery of GAGs (and perhaps also other compounds) to lysosomes, preventing their effective turnover.
evidence.explanation: States the pivotal causal step explicitly: low VPS33A causes defective endosomal trafficking and poor delivery of GAGs to lysosomes, preventing turnover - a delivery failure rather than a catabolic block. Evidence source is OTHER because this sentence is the paper's background synthesis of prior work, not a result of its own experiments.

steps/3.description: With HOPS and CORVET depleted, the tethering and fusion events that carry endocytic cargo from early through late endosomes into the lysosome become inefficient. Patient fibroblasts show vacuolation with disordered endosomal/lysosomal compartments, elevated EEA1 (required at early/late endosome fusion and early-endosome sorting), altered Golgi morphology, and abnormal endocytic trafficking of lactosylceramide and other glycosphingolipids. This node is the mechanistic pivot of MPSPS: it is a delivery failure upstream of catabolism, not a catabolic block, and it is what distinguishes MPSPS from every classical mucopolysaccharidosis.

evidence.snippet: Patients with MPSPS exhibited excessive excretion of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) in the urine and exceptionally high levels of heparan sulfate in the plasma, but the accumulation of substrates is not caused by a decrease in the activity of any lysosomal enzymes.
evidence.explanation: The single most important statement for this entry: GAG storage occurs without any decrease in lysosomal enzyme activity. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a focused review synthesising several study types.

evidence.snippet: They showed extremely high levels of plasma heparan sulphate (HS, one of GAG); 60 times the normal reference range and 6 times that of MPS patients.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the magnitude of heparan sulphate accumulation in MPSPS, which exceeds that of classical MPS.

evidence.snippet: We hence propose a new type of MPS that is not caused by an enzymatic deficiency.
evidence.explanation: The original description explicitly frames MPSPS as an MPS-like storage disease that is not caused by an enzymatic deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Urine glycosaminoglycan studies revealed a pathological excess of sialylated conjugates as well as dermatan and heparan sulphate.
evidence.explanation: Characterises the stored/excreted species as dermatan and heparan sulphate plus sialylated conjugates.

evidence.snippet: Lipidomic screening showed elevated β-D-galactosylsphingosine with unimpaired activity of cognate lysosomal hydrolases.
evidence.explanation: Documents accumulation of a lipid species alongside explicitly unimpaired cognate lysosomal hydrolase activity.

evidence.snippet: a weak HS colocalisation with LysoTracker Red
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the conformance asserted on this node: heparan sulphate shows only weak colocalisation with an acidic-lysosome marker in MPSPS fibroblasts, so the storage compartment may be endosomal rather than the lysosomal lumen the module's accumulation node presumes. The quote supports storage itself while qualifying its classical intralysosomal localisation.

steps/4.description: Heparan, dermatan and (variably) chondroitin sulphate accumulate and are excreted in excess in the urine, and plasma heparan sulphate is extraordinarily elevated - around 60 times the normal reference range and six times the level seen in classical MPS patients. Sialylated conjugates, sialooligosaccharides, elevated beta-D-galactosylsphingosine and cholesterol and sphingolipid abnormalities are also reported. The defining biochemical signature of MPSPS is that all of this occurs with entirely normal activity of the cognate lysosomal hydrolases: it is substrate accumulation without an enzyme deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Lysosomal over-acidification and HS accumulation were detected in patient-derived and VPS33A-depleted cells, suggesting a novel role of this gene in lysosomal functions.
evidence.explanation: Establishes lysosomal over-acidification together with heparan sulphate accumulation as the cellular readout in MPSPS cells.

evidence.snippet: As in the infantile form of mucopolysaccharidosis plus, the endocytic compartment in the fibroblasts also expanded-a phenomenon accompanied by increased endolysosomal acidification and impaired intracellular glycosphingolipid trafficking.
evidence.explanation: Independently replicates endocytic compartment expansion and increased endolysosomal acidification in the second VPS33A variant.

evidence.snippet: elevated levels of the LC3-II and p62 proteins (autophagy markers)
evidence.explanation: Supports an autophagic-flux abnormality in MPSPS fibroblasts, though the finding rests on a single p.Arg200Pro cell line and the original p.Arg498Trp study reported no autophagic defect (see the autophagy-discrepancy discussion).

evidence.snippet: VPS33A is involved in endocytic and autophagic pathways, but the identified mutation did not affect either of these pathways.
evidence.explanation: Retained deliberately as counter-evidence: the original p.Arg498Trp study found no measurable effect on the endocytic or autophagic pathways in patient skin fibroblasts, which is in tension with the later p.Arg200Pro autophagy-marker findings. The disagreement is recorded as an open knowledge gap rather than silently resolved.

steps/5.description: Failed tethering and fusion leave an expanded endocytic compartment that is abnormally acidified. Lysosomal over-acidification was detected in patient-derived and VPS33A-depleted cells in the original description, and increased endolysosomal acidification with an expanded endocytic compartment was independently confirmed in the juvenile p.Arg200Pro form. Autophagy markers LC3-II and p62 are elevated in p.Arg200Pro fibroblasts, indicating a block in autophagic flux, though the original p.Arg498Trp study did not detect an autophagic defect (see the autophagy-discrepancy discussion below).

evidence.snippet: Histological analyses of MPSPS kidneys similarly suggest the extensive destruction of glomerular structures by foamy podocytes.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents foamy (storage-laden) podocytes destroying glomerular structures in MPSPS kidneys.

evidence.snippet: High urinary excretion of protein (caused by impairments in renal filtration), hypoalbuminemia, and elevated levels of creatinine, cholesterol, and uric acid indicate renal dysfunction.
evidence.explanation: Links the podocyte/glomerular lesion to the measured renal phenotype: proteinuria from impaired filtration, hypoalbuminaemia and azotaemia.

evidence.snippet: Renal biopsy showed segmental sclerosis, periglomerular fibrosis and inflammatory cell infiltration.
evidence.explanation: Provides the biopsy evidence for the periglomerular fibrosis and interstitial inflammation described on this node.

steps/6.description: The kidney is one of the two most discriminating "plus" targets. Storage in podocytes converts them to foam cells and destroys glomerular architecture, producing nephrotic-range proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia, and rising creatinine, cholesterol and uric acid. Histology shows extensive destruction of glomerular structures by foamy podocytes, with periglomerular fibrosis and interstitial inflammation.

evidence.snippet: Bone marrow aspiration analysis showed hypoplastic bone marrow without any storage cells.
evidence.explanation: Key negative finding: the marrow is hypoplastic yet free of storage cells, which is why this node is deliberately not mapped to the module's storage-cell node and why the mechanism of the cytopenias is unresolved.

evidence.snippet: A series of blood tests indicate hematopoietic symptoms including progressive anemia and thrombocytopenia, which correlate with histological observations of hypoplastic bone marrow.
evidence.explanation: Connects the peripheral cytopenias to a hypoplastic marrow, establishing the marrow as the site of the haematopoietic lesion.

evidence.snippet: A rare lysosomal disease resembling a mucopolysaccharidosis with unusual systemic features, including renal disease and platelet dysfunction, caused by the defect in a conserved region of the VPS33A gene on human chromosome 12q24.31, occurs in Yakuts
evidence.explanation: Identifies renal disease and platelet dysfunction as the unusual systemic features distinguishing this disorder from a conventional MPS. Indirect because platelet dysfunction is a qualitative platelet defect, not the marrow hypoplasia and quantitative cytopenias this node models.

steps/7.description: The haematopoietic system is the second discriminating "plus" target. edges/1.description: Loss of intact VPS33A, a core subunit of both complexes, secondarily lowers the abundance of the other HOPS and CORVET components.

edges/2.description: Depletion of the tethering complexes impairs the membrane tethering and fusion steps of the endocytic route to the lysosome.

edges/3.description: GAGs that are not efficiently delivered to the lysosome are not turned over and accumulate in cells, despite intact degradative enzymes.

edges/4.description: Failed fusion leaves an expanded, abnormally acidified endolysosomal compartment.

edges/5.description: Progressive intracellular storage across many tissues produces the MPS-like plus multisystem clinical picture.

evidence.snippet: Histological analyses of MPSPS kidneys similarly suggest the extensive destruction of glomerular structures by foamy podocytes.
evidence.explanation: The foamy (storage-laden) podocyte is itself the histological readout of substrate accumulation in this cell type; indirect because the quote documents the storage cell rather than tracing the loading step.

edges/6.description: Accumulating undegraded material loads the podocyte, the one unambiguous storage cell in MPSPS, converting it into the foam cell that destroys glomerular architecture.

edges/7.description: Urinary GAG excess is the direct overflow of the accumulating undegraded substrate and the finding that first suggests a mucopolysaccharidosis.

evidence.snippet: These results suggested that dysfunction of VPS33A protein leads to GAG accumulation and causes MPS-like phenotypes.
evidence.explanation: The sources attribute the MPS-like cluster, of which coarse facies is an enumerated member, to GAG accumulation. Evidence source is OTHER because this is the review's synthesis sentence; indirect because the attribution is to the cluster, not this phenotype individually.

edges/8.description: Coarse facies is one of the enumerated MPS-like manifestations attributed to GAG accumulation; the tissue-level intermediates have not been demonstrated in MPSPS.

edges/9.description: Macroglossia is listed as a component of the MPSPS coarse-facies complex; it shares the storage attribution evidenced on the coarse facial features edge.

edges/17.description: Sustained endolysosomal dysfunction drives cell-type-specific injury and progressive organ disease.

edges/18.description: Glomerular destruction contributes the renal arm of the plus phenotype.

evidence.snippet: High urinary excretion of protein (caused by impairments in renal filtration), hypoalbuminemia, and elevated levels of creatinine, cholesterol, and uric acid indicate renal dysfunction.
evidence.explanation: The parenthetical states the causal mechanism of the proteinuria directly: impaired renal filtration, the functional consequence of the glomerular destruction this node models.

edges/19.description: Destruction of the glomerular filtration barrier by foamy podocytes lets protein pass into the urine.

edges/20.description: Glomerular destruction by foamy podocytes produces the full nephrotic picture of heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia and oedema seen in the majority of patients.

edges/21.description: Hypoalbuminaemia follows from the heavy urinary protein loss caused by the glomerular lesion.

edges/22.description: Marrow failure contributes the haematopoietic arm of the plus phenotype.

edges/23.description: Marrow hypocellularity on aspiration is the direct histological readout of the hypoplastic marrow this node models.

edges/24.description: Underproduction by the hypoplastic marrow drives the progressive anaemia, which correlates with the histological marrow findings.

edges/25.description: Underproduction by the hypoplastic marrow drives the progressive thrombocytopenia, which correlates with the histological marrow findings.

edges/26.description: Leukocytopenia is the third lineage of the multilineage cytopenia arising from the hypoplastic marrow.

evidence.snippet: We observed that the missense mutation reduced the abundance of full-length VPS33A and other components of the HOPS and CORVET complexes.
evidence.explanation: Supports the statement that the missense allele depletes not only VPS33A but the other HOPS/CORVET components, the molecular basis for the disproportionate effect of a single missense change.

evidence.snippet: To our knowledge this is the first report of an attenuated juvenile form of VPS33A insufficiency characterized by appreciable residual endosomal-lysosomal trafficking and a milder mucopolysaccharidosis plus than the disease in infants.
evidence.explanation: Supports the genotype-phenotype correlation: residual trafficking capacity distinguishes the attenuated p.Arg200Pro course from the lethal infantile p.Arg498Trp disease.

evidence.snippet: Using whole exome and Sanger sequencing, we identified homozygous c.1492C > T (p.Arg498Trp) mutations in the VPS33A gene of 13 patients.
evidence.explanation: Original gene discovery: homozygous VPS33A p.Arg498Trp in 13 patients by exome and Sanger sequencing.

evidence.snippet: Up to now, a total number of 39 patients have been reported; in all of them, the c.1492C>T (p.Arg498Trp) variant of the VPS33A gene was detected.
evidence.explanation: Confirms p.Arg498Trp as the recurrent allele across the whole reported cohort at that time.

evidence.snippet: We describe an attenuated juvenile form of VPS33A-related syndrome-mucopolysaccharidosis plus in a man who is homozygous for a hitherto unknown missense mutation (NM_022916.4: c.599 G>C; NP_075067.2:p. Arg200Pro) in a conserved region of the VPS33A gene.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the second pathogenic VPS33A allele and its association with the attenuated juvenile phenotype.

genes/0.notes: Variant class and mechanism: both known alleles are germline homozygous MISSENSE substitutions in conserved regions, acting as hypomorphic loss of function through protein instability - NOT nonsense, frameshift, whole-gene deletion, gain of function or dominant negative. No CNV, structural, somatic or mosaic mechanism has been implicated, and no modifier gene is known. Because VPS33A is a shared core subunit, the molecular consequence extends beyond VPS33A itself: patient cells show secondary reduction of the other HOPS/CORVET components (VPS18, VPS41), so a single missense allele depletes two multi-subunit complexes. Penetrance and genotype-phenotype: penetrance of homozygous p.Arg498Trp appears complete in reported families, with no formal age-dependent penetrance estimate published. The genotype-phenotype correlation is the clearest feature of the MPSPS genetics - p.Arg498Trp gives the lethal infantile disease while p.Arg200Pro gives an attenuated juvenile course, attributed to appreciable RESIDUAL endosomal-lysosomal trafficking rather than to any qualitative difference in mechanism. Caveat: the p.Arg200Pro correlation rests on only two reported patients. Founder allele: p.Arg498Trp is a Yakut founder allele with a carrier frequency of 1:81 and a birth incidence of about 1 per 12,100 in that population (see prevalence). Consanguinity is not required - the original Yakut series comprised children of healthy, non-consanguineous parents - although the two Turkish patients were born to first cousins.

evidence.snippet: Currently there is no specific therapy for this disease and clinical management is limited to supportive and symptomatic treatment.
evidence.explanation: States that no specific therapy exists and management is supportive and symptomatic.

treatments/0.description: There is no approved disease-modifying therapy for MPSPS, and enzyme replacement is not a logical strategy because no single hydrolase is deficient. Management is multidisciplinary and supportive: airway clearance, oxygen and ventilatory support, prompt antibiotics for respiratory infection, nutritional and developmental support, standard cardiac and renal management, transfusion for significant cytopenia, and surveillance of cardiac, renal, respiratory, haematologic, hearing and vision status.

evidence.snippet: Currently there is no specific therapy for this disease and clinical management is limited to supportive and symptomatic treatment.
evidence.explanation: Supports supportive/symptomatic management as the standard of care. Indirect because the quoted sentence establishes the supportive-care principle without itemising the specific respiratory interventions.

treatments/1.description: Airway clearance and bronchial drainage, supplemental oxygen and ventilatory support as required, and prompt antibiotics for bacterial respiratory infection. This is the highest-yield supportive axis because recurrent respiratory infection from 2-6 months of age is the usual presenting problem and cardiorespiratory failure is the usual mode of death.

evidence.snippet: A series of blood tests indicate hematopoietic symptoms including progressive anemia and thrombocytopenia, which correlate with histological observations of hypoplastic bone marrow.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the progressive anaemia and thrombocytopenia that create the transfusion requirement. Indirect because it documents the indication rather than reporting transfusion outcomes.

treatments/2.description: Red-cell or platelet transfusion for clinically significant anaemia or thrombocytopenia arising from the hypoplastic marrow. Purely supportive: it does not address the underlying marrow hypoplasia, whose mechanism is unexplained given the documented absence of marrow storage cells.

evidence.snippet: The prolonged steroid treatment allowed a stabilization of his general and hematological conditions and probably determined an improvement of his psychomotor milestones and new neurological acquisitions with an improvement of quality of life.
evidence.explanation: Reports the observed benefit; note this is a single uncontrolled case and the authors themselves describe the effect as probable.

treatments/3.description: In a single unusually long-surviving child who developed secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis at two years of age, steroids treated the HLH successfully and a very prolonged course was associated with stabilisation of general and haematological status. This is a single case report; corticosteroids are NOT established MPSPS therapy and the authors themselves state the approach deserves further investigation.

evidence.snippet: Consequently, a placental biopsy was performed, leading to an early diagnosis of MPSPS.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates feasibility of targeted prenatal molecular diagnosis once parental carrier status is known.

evidence.snippet: During their pregnancies, both women underwent prenatal ultrasonography, which revealed increased prenasal thickness during the second trimester.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the sonographic marker that can trigger prenatal genetic testing.

treatments/4.description: Because MPSPS is autosomal recessive with a defined founder allele, cascade carrier testing, nondirective counselling and targeted prenatal diagnosis (chorionic villus/placental biopsy DNA when the familial variant is known) are the principal preventive options. Increased prenasal thickness on second-trimester ultrasonography can prompt testing in families with no known history.

evidence.snippet: Exposure of patient-derived fibroblasts to the clinically approved proteasome inhibitor, bortezomib, or inhibition of glucosylceramide synthesis with eliglustat, partially corrected the impaired lactosylceramide trafficking defect and immediately suggest therapeutic avenues to explore in this fatal orphan disease.
evidence.explanation: Reports partial in vitro correction of a trafficking defect; a cell-culture result with no clinical evidence of benefit.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrated that treatment with genistein and ambroxol resulted in elevation of the mutant VPS33A protein level, as well as in improvement or correction of various previously reported cellular defects, including GAG levels, endosomal markers, and cytoskeleton elements
evidence.explanation: Reports in vitro rescue of mutant VPS33A abundance and multiple downstream cellular defects; the evidence is a single patient-derived fibroblast line with no clinical data.

treatments/5.description: Because the disease mechanism is destabilisation and degradation of a partially functional VPS33A protein rather than absence of catalytic activity, raising the steady-state level of the mutant protein is a rational strategy. In patient-derived fibroblasts the proteasome inhibitor bortezomib (and, separately, the glucosylceramide-synthase inhibitor eliglustat) partially corrected the lactosylceramide trafficking defect, and the proteasome inhibitor genistein combined with the ERAD inhibitor ambroxol raised mutant VPS33A levels and corrected GAG, endosomal-marker and cytoskeletal defects. All of this is IN VITRO only. No clinical trial exists, and bortezomib's toxicity makes off-label use unsupported outside formal research.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, we asked the question whether MPSPS should be classified as a type of MPS or a separate disease, as contrary to 'classical' MPS types, despite GAG accumulation, no defects in lysosomal enzymes responsible for degradation of these compounds could be detected in MPSPS.
evidence.explanation: The 2024 review poses exactly this nosological question and states the reason it is unresolved.

open_questions/0.rationale: GAG storage and MPS-like clinical features argue for inclusion among the mucopolysaccharidoses; normal lysosomal GAG-hydrolase activity and a primary membrane-tethering/trafficking lesion argue for a separate entity. The question is not merely terminological: it determines whether MPSPS belongs in the Mucopolysaccharidoses grouping (whose rationale requires deficiency of a GAG-degrading enzyme) and whether newborn screening by enzyme assay could ever detect it. This entry takes the position that MPSPS is a lysosomal storage disorder reached by a trafficking route, hence downstream-only conformance to lysosomal_substrate_accumulation and no MPS-grouping membership on the criteria as currently written.

evidence.snippet: VPS33A is involved in endocytic and autophagic pathways, but the identified mutation did not affect either of these pathways.
evidence.explanation: The negative finding in p.Arg498Trp fibroblasts that generates the discrepancy.

evidence.snippet: elevated levels of the LC3-II and p62 proteins (autophagy markers)
evidence.explanation: The positive autophagy-marker finding in p.Arg200Pro fibroblasts that conflicts with the earlier negative result.

open_questions/1.rationale: The original p.Arg498Trp study explicitly reported that the mutation did NOT affect the endocytic or autophagic pathways in patient skin fibroblasts, whereas a later study of p.Arg200Pro fibroblasts found elevated LC3-II and p62, indicating a block in autophagic flux. Because HOPS is required for autophagosome-lysosome fusion, an autophagy defect is mechanistically expected, making the negative result surprising. Resolving this matters for whether the Autophagic-Lysosomal Dysfunction conformance asserted here is correct for both variants, and for whether autophagy-modulating therapy is rational.

open_questions/2.rationale: Patient-derived skin fibroblasts and HeLa cells reproduce VPS33A depletion, HOPS/CORVET loss, endolysosomal disorganisation and trafficking defects, but they cannot model the cardiorespiratory, renal-podocyte, marrow-hypoplasia or neurodevelopmental phenotypes. In particular the causal edge from GAG storage to congenital heart disease is asserted clinically but has never been demonstrated experimentally in any system, and the in vitro drug rescues (bortezomib, eliglustat, genistein/ambroxol) are all fibroblast readouts of uncertain organ-level relevance. No validated VPS33A p.Arg498Trp knock-in mouse, zebrafish, organoid or iPSC model recapitulating the human syndrome has been reported.

evidence.snippet: It is still unknown how missense mutation p.R498W in VPS33A cause accumulation of GAGs. Detailed mechanism and disease pathophysiology remain to be elucidated.
evidence.explanation: The disease review states outright that the pathophysiology beyond the trafficking lesion is unresolved, which is the reason these phenotypes carry no causal edge.

open_questions/3.rationale: These phenotypes are deliberately left without incoming causal edges. The marrow precedent shows why manufacturing storage edges would be wrong: MPSPS marrow is hypoplastic yet contains no storage cells, so at least one major MPSPS organ phenotype is demonstrably NOT storage-cell-driven, and the same may be true of any phenotype in this list. Per cluster: the congenital heart lesions (ASD, PDA) are established at birth, before substantial postnatal storage, and the valve regurgitation that is storage-attributed in classical MPS has no MPSPS valve histology to support the same attribution; ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary hypertension are plausibly haemodynamic consequences of the valve disease, but no source asserts that chain. Delayed CNS myelination and basal ganglia calcification are not classical MPS features, so the MPS-phenocopy attribution to GAG accumulation does not extend to them; hypotonia and nystagmus have no localising pathology. The IgM-high/IgG-low pattern could reflect selective urinary IgG loss in the nephrotic state, but no MPSPS source makes that link. Retinal hypopigmentation is intriguing given that the Vps33a-mutant buff mouse models Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome with oculocutaneous albinism, suggesting a lysosome-related-organelle route, but this has not been examined in patients. Secondary HLH is a single case, and fetal ascites and nephromegaly are reported without any mechanistic account. The mpsps_no_organ_level_model discussion records the corresponding absence of any organ-level experimental system in which these mechanisms could be tested.

evidence.snippet: Unlike other human cancers, in which all primary tumors arise de novo, ovarian epithelial cancers are primarily imported from either endometrial or fallopian tube epithelium.
evidence.explanation: This review-level synthesis supports a tubal epithelial origin model for the serous ovarian cancers curated in this entry.

steps/2.description: The dominant current model places HGSOC origin in the distal fallopian tube rather than the ovarian surface epithelium. Secretory/non-ciliated epithelial cells in the fimbria provide the main human cell-of-origin framework for the disease.

evidence.snippet: Mathematical models imply that a prolonged time (decades) elapses from the development of a TP53 mutation, the earliest known molecular alteration, to an STIC, followed by a shorter span (6 years) for progression to an HGSC.
evidence.explanation: This supports TP53 mutation as the earliest recurrent lesion in the canonical human tubal precursor sequence.

evidence.snippet: Here we report that high-grade serous ovarian cancer is characterized by TP53 mutations in almost all tumours (96%)
evidence.explanation: TCGA confirms that TP53 alteration remains near-universal in invasive HGSOC.

steps/3.description: TP53 alteration is the earliest and nearly universal lesion in HGSOC. TP53-mutant tubal epithelial precursor fields create the genomic context from which STIC and invasive carcinoma emerge.

evidence.snippet: In contrast, pre-ciliated cells (Krt5+, Prom1+, Trp73+) remain cancer-prone and give rise to serous tubal intraepithelial carcinomas and overt HGSC.
evidence.explanation: Mouse lineage-tracing and transformation experiments support a distinct cancer-prone transitional tubal epithelial cell state upstream of STIC and HGSC.

steps/4.description: Recent functional modeling suggests that a pre-ciliated tubal epithelial state is especially permissive for HGSOC initiation after combined TP53 and RB1 pathway loss. This complements, rather than replaces, the dominant human secretory-cell origin model.

evidence.snippet: The precancerous landscape in fallopian tubes contains multiple concurrent precursor lesions, including serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), with genetic heterogeneity providing a platform for HGSC evolution.
evidence.explanation: This supports STIC as the principal tubal precursor lesion that seeds invasive HGSOC evolution.

steps/5.description: STIC is the best-established morphologic precursor lesion for most HGSOCs and provides the bridge between TP53-mutant tubal epithelium and invasive extrauterine serous carcinoma.

evidence.snippet: All PARPis showed significant benefit, with olaparib showing greater benefit in newly diagnosed and PSR OC women.
evidence.explanation: This supports the clinically important BRCA-associated HRD subset in metastatic ovarian cancer.

evidence.snippet: Pathway analyses suggested that homologous recombination is defective in about half of the tumours analysed
evidence.explanation: TCGA establishes HRD as a central, not peripheral, mechanism in HGSOC biology.

steps/6.description: Roughly half of HGSOC demonstrates defective homologous recombination repair through BRCA1/2 mutation, BRCA1 promoter methylation, or other HR-pathway lesions. HRD creates genomic scarring, underlies platinum sensitivity, and instantiates the trigger node of the DNA-repair synthetic-lethality module — making HGSOC the prototypical disease for PARP inhibitor synthetic lethality.

evidence.snippet: PARP inhibition causes synthetic lethality in breast cancers associated with germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations and is routinely used in clinical practice for metastatic breast cancer.
evidence.explanation: Review evidence supports PARP-inhibitor synthetic lethality in BRCA-associated tumors; HGSOC is the cancer for which this paradigm is most clinically established.

evidence.snippet: At 7 years, 67.0% of olaparib patients versus 46.5% of placebo patients were alive, and 45.3% versus 20.6%, respectively, were alive and had not received a first subsequent treatment
evidence.explanation: SOLO1 long-term survival data are the clinical embodiment of PARP-platinum synthetic lethality in BRCA-associated HGSOC.

steps/7.description: In HRD-positive HGSOC, PARP inhibition blocks single-strand break repair and converts unresolved lesions into double-strand breaks that cannot be faithfully repaired, while platinum agents add interstrand crosslinks that similarly stress HRR and FA/BRCA repair. This is the canonical synthetic-lethal exploitation that drives durable maintenance olaparib benefit in BRCA-associated and HRD-positive first-line HGSOC.

evidence.snippet: Among reversions mediated by frameshift deletions, 60% are flanked by DNA microhomologies, implicating POLQ-mediated repair.
evidence.explanation: TOPARP-B post-progression sequencing connects microhomology-flanked reversion events to POLQ-mediated repair, supporting POLQ as the escape polymerase under PARP-inhibitor pressure in HRD tumors including HGSOC.

evidence.snippet: We find that TINS consistent with TMEJ repair are highly specific to tumors with pathogenic biallelic mutations in BRCA2 and that high TINS genomic signature content in advanced ovarian cancers associate with overall survival following treatment with platinum agents.
evidence.explanation: Ovarian evidence that this node is actually active in the disease. A templated-insertion signature attributable to theta-mediated end joining is specific to biallelic BRCA2 tumors, and its burden in advanced ovarian cancer tracks survival after platinum. This establishes TMEJ activity in BRCA2-deficient HGSOC; it does not show that TMEJ produced any particular reversion allele.

evidence.snippet: Emerging DNA double-strand breaks are repaired via an error-prone mechanism in which the outermost nucleotide of one end serves to prime DNA synthesis on the other end. This pathway critically depends on the A-family polymerase theta, which protects the genome against gross chromosomal rearrangements.
evidence.explanation: The causal anchor under an otherwise correlative node. Genetic work in C. elegans shows the microhomology-flanked deletion class at replication-associated breaks depends on polymerase theta, which the human signature data cannot establish. Two extrapolations still separate this from the clinical claim: species, and deletion class versus reversion at a BRCA locus under drug pressure.

steps/8.description: Under PARP-inhibitor or platinum pressure, HRD HGSOC cells can rely on POLQ (DNA polymerase theta) and microhomology-mediated end joining to survive double-strand breaks that HRR cannot resolve. POLQ-mediated repair is error-prone and can itself generate the microhomology-flanked frameshift deletions that produce BRCA reversion events. POLQ is largely dispensable in normal cells, making it a candidate pivot point for second-line synthetic lethality. TMEJ activity in ovarian tumors is most clearly established in biallelic BRCA2 disease, where a templated-insertion signature is both specific to BRCA2 loss and associated with survival after platinum.

evidence.snippet: No baseline BRCA reversion mutations were observed in 100 BRCA+ patients. NGS identified somatic BRCA reversion mutations in 39% (39/100) of patients after progression.
evidence.explanation: TRITON2 post-progression plasma analysis directly documents acquired BRCA reversion mutations after PARP-inhibitor treatment, the canonical restored-HRR resistance pathway (demonstrated here in BRCA-associated cancer and shared by BRCA-mutant HGSOC).

evidence.snippet: These data support the need for restored HRR function in PARPi resistance.
evidence.explanation: TOPARP-B resistance analysis supports restored HRR as a requirement for PARP-inhibitor resistance in HRD tumors.

steps/9.description: Resistant HGSOC subclones can acquire BRCA1 or BRCA2 reversion mutations that restore open reading frames and re-establish HRR function. Once HRR is restored, PARP-inhibitor and platinum sensitivity are lost and the synthetic-lethal relationship is broken. Reversion alleles are detectable in circulating tumor DNA at progression and are the principal mechanism of acquired PARP-inhibitor resistance in BRCA-associated HGSOC.

evidence.snippet: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma is a unique cancer characterised by universal TP53 mutations and widespread copy number alterations.
evidence.explanation: This review-level synthesis succinctly captures the defining copy-number-driven genomic architecture of HGSOC.

evidence.snippet: Here we report that high-grade serous ovarian cancer is characterized by TP53 mutations in almost all tumours (96%); low prevalence but statistically recurrent somatic mutations in nine further genes including NF1, BRCA1, BRCA2, RB1 and CDK12; 113 significant focal DNA copy number aberrations
evidence.explanation: TCGA directly documents the high focal copy-number alteration burden that defines HGSOC.

steps/10.description: HGSOC is a copy-number driven carcinoma with extensive focal amplifications, deletions, aneuploidy, and structural rearrangement. This genomic architecture distinguishes it from point-mutation-dominated carcinomas.

evidence.snippet: Forty-four genes are found to have evidence as amplified therapeutic targets; the five highest scoring genes are CCNE1, PAX8, URI1, PRKCI and FAL1.
evidence.explanation: This review identifies CCNE1 as one of the strongest amplified therapeutic target candidates in HGSOC.

steps/11.description: CCNE1 amplification is a recurrent copy-number event in HGSOC that reinforces G1/S progression and replication stress. It marks a clinically important copy-number-driven subset with adverse therapeutic implications.

steps/12.description: The combined effects of TP53 dysfunction, HRD-associated genomic damage, and recurrent cell-cycle driver amplification converge on sustained malignant proliferation of serous epithelial tumor cells.

evidence.snippet: In ovarian cancer, this shift may be one of the reasons the disease spreads so readily and comes back despite intensive treatment.
evidence.explanation: This supports EMT as a contributor to ovarian cancer dissemination and recurrence after treatment.

steps/13.description: EMT-like transcriptional programs facilitate detachment, invasion, and mesothelial implantation, while also contributing to treatment resistance and recurrence.

evidence.snippet: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) dissemination is primarily mediated by the shedding of tumor cells from the primary site into ascites where they form multicellular spheroids that rapidly lead to peritoneal carcinomatosis.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports the dominant transcoelomic mechanism of ovarian cancer metastasis.

steps/14.description: Ovarian cancer typically metastasizes by shedding into ascites rather than first through the bloodstream. Tumor cells form multicellular spheroids that survive in suspension and implant across peritoneal surfaces.

evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, OCAMs can induce decreased platinum-sensitivity in OvCa cells via induction of the FN1/Akt signaling pathway via cell-to-cell interactions.
evidence.explanation: This supports a direct microenvironmental mechanism of platinum resistance in peritoneal metastasis.

steps/15.description: Disseminated ovarian cancer cells engage mesothelial and stromal cells within the peritoneum, creating FN1-AKT and related survival programs that protect tumor cells from platinum-induced apoptosis.

evidence.snippet: Most patients with advanced-stage ovarian cancer receive maintenance therapy with bevacizumab (a monoclonal antibody that blocks angiogenesis) and/or poly-adenosine diphosphate ribose polymerase (PARP) inhibitors.
evidence.explanation: The clinical use of bevacizumab maintenance therapy supports angiogenesis as a key dependency of advanced ovarian cancer.

steps/16.description: Ovarian cancer metastases depend on angiogenic support within the peritoneal cavity, and anti-VEGF therapy remains part of maintenance treatment for advanced-stage disease.

evidence.snippet: Consequently, the high abundance of these cells often leads to immunosuppression, tumor growth, treatment failure, and poor prognosis.
evidence.explanation: This ovarian cancer review supports immune evasion through accumulation of immunosuppressive myeloid-derived suppressor cells in the tumor microenvironment.

steps/17.description: Metastatic ovarian cancer develops an immunosuppressive microenvironment in which myeloid-derived suppressor cells accumulate and blunt antitumor immune responses.

edges/4.description: Tubal epithelial precursor fields acquire the earliest recurrent genetic lesion.

edges/5.description: TP53-mutant precursor fields progress to overt intraepithelial carcinoma.

edges/6.description: Loss of p53 constraint permits accumulation of structural genomic damage.

edges/7.description: Transformation-prone tubal epithelial states can generate STIC lesions.

edges/8.description: Progression to invasive HGSOC is accompanied by pervasive genomic instability.

edges/9.description: HR repair failure promotes structural genomic damage and genomic scarring.

edges/10.description: HRD creates the synthetic-lethal vulnerability that PARP inhibitors and platinum agents exploit.

edges/11.description: Treatment pressure can select tumor cells that survive by switching to POLQ-mediated alternative end-joining.

edges/12.description: Resistant subclones can also acquire BRCA reversion mutations that restore HRR and lose the synthetic-lethal vulnerability.

edges/13.description: Microhomology-mediated repair generates the frameshift-deletion reversion events that restore HRR gene reading frames.

edges/14.description: Recurrent amplification of cell-cycle drivers emerges within the unstable genome.

edges/15.description: CCNE1 amplification reinforces rapid cell-cycle entry and tumor growth.

edges/16.description: Sustained proliferation of the established tumour supplies the cell population in which EMT-like transcriptional programs arise.

edges/17.description: The peritoneal metastatic niche accumulates myeloid-derived suppressor cells, blunting antitumour immunity against the disseminated tumour.

edges/18.description: Peritoneal implants depend on angiogenic support for outgrowth, the basis for anti-VEGF maintenance therapy in advanced disease.

edges/19.description: Disseminated cells and spheroids engage mesothelial and stromal cells on peritoneal surfaces, establishing the survival programs that blunt platinum sensitivity.

edges/20.description: EMT-like programs drive detachment from the primary lesion, allowing shed cells to form the multicellular spheroids that seed the peritoneum.

evidence.snippet: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma is a unique cancer characterised by universal TP53 mutations and widespread copy number alterations.
evidence.explanation: This supports TP53 mutation as the foundational, near-universal genetic lesion in HGSOC.

evidence.snippet: Here we report that high-grade serous ovarian cancer is characterized by TP53 mutations in almost all tumours (96%)
evidence.explanation: TCGA directly supports near-universal TP53 mutation in HGSOC.

genes/0.notes: TP53 mutation is the defining recurrent genetic lesion of HGSOC and a cornerstone of the tubal precursor-to-carcinoma progression model.

evidence.snippet: Hereditary factors are associated with 25% of cases, predominantly linked to BRCA1/2 gene variants.
evidence.explanation: This supports BRCA1 as a major hereditary driver of ovarian cancer.

evidence.snippet: Here we report that high-grade serous ovarian cancer is characterized by TP53 mutations in almost all tumours (96%); low prevalence but statistically recurrent somatic mutations in nine further genes including NF1, BRCA1, BRCA2, RB1 and CDK12; 113 significant focal DNA copy number aberrations
evidence.explanation: TCGA documents recurrent BRCA1 alteration within HGSOC.

genes/1.notes: BRCA1 loss contributes to HRD through germline mutation, somatic mutation, or promoter hypermethylation and is clinically linked to platinum and PARP inhibitor sensitivity.

evidence.snippet: Here we report that high-grade serous ovarian cancer is characterized by TP53 mutations in almost all tumours (96%); low prevalence but statistically recurrent somatic mutations in nine further genes including NF1, BRCA1, BRCA2, RB1 and CDK12; 113 significant focal DNA copy number aberrations
evidence.explanation: TCGA documents recurrent BRCA2 alteration within HGSOC.

genes/2.notes: BRCA2 loss is a core HRD mechanism in HGSOC and supports the clinically important BRCA-associated facet of the disease.

evidence.snippet: Forty-four genes are found to have evidence as amplified therapeutic targets; the five highest scoring genes are CCNE1, PAX8, URI1, PRKCI and FAL1.
evidence.explanation: This supports CCNE1 as the top-ranked amplified driver oncogene in HGSOC.

evidence.snippet: Forty-four genes are found to have evidence as amplified therapeutic targets; the five highest scoring genes are CCNE1, PAX8, URI1, PRKCI and FAL1.
evidence.explanation: This supports CCNE1 amplification as a recurrent driver lesion in HGSOC.

genes/3.notes: CCNE1 amplification is a hallmark copy-number event in a clinically important subset of HGSOC.

evidence.snippet: Advanced-stage ovarian cancer may be treated with primary cytoreductive surgery (removal of all visible cancer in the abdominal cavity) and adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin and paclitaxel) or with neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by cytoreductive surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports carboplatin/paclitaxel as the standard systemic backbone in advanced ovarian cancer, the clinical context dominated by HGSOC.

treatments/0.description: Platinum-taxane chemotherapy remains the first-line systemic backbone for HGSOC in both adjuvant and advanced-stage settings.

evidence.snippet: In this scenario, standard treatment includes a combination of cytoreductive surgery and carboplatinum–paclitaxel-based chemotherapy.
evidence.explanation: Direct statement of the first-line standard of care for advanced-stage disease, which is the intervention the other treatments in this entry modify or are added to.

evidence.snippet: Advanced-stage ovarian cancer may be treated with primary cytoreductive surgery (removal of all visible cancer in the abdominal cavity) and adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin and paclitaxel) or with neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by cytoreductive surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy.
evidence.explanation: This supports cytoreductive surgery as a standard first-line procedure in advanced ovarian cancer care.

treatments/1.description: Cytoreductive surgery remains a core component of first-line HGSOC management in patients who are candidates for primary or interval debulking.

evidence.snippet: Olaparib | Accepted_Therapeutic_Use_For | - | - | deleterious or suspected deleterious germline or somatic BRCA-mutated (gBRCAm or sBRCAm) advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer; deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA-mutated (gBRCAm), HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer
evidence.explanation: NCI Thesaurus asserts accepted therapeutic use of olaparib for BRCA-mutated advanced epithelial ovarian cancer.

evidence.snippet: Among ovarian cancer patients with BRCA mutation or homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), the efficacy of Poly-ADP-ribose polymerase (PARP) inhibitors such as olaparib, niraparib, veliparib, and rucaparib has been proven in a number of clinical trials.
evidence.explanation: Review-level synthesis supports PARP inhibitor maintenance as a treatment class for BRCA-mutated or HRD ovarian cancer; carried over from the folded Metastatic_Ovarian_Cancer entry.

evidence.snippet: At 7 years, 67.0% of olaparib patients versus 46.5% of placebo patients were alive, and 45.3% versus 20.6%, respectively, were alive and had not received a first subsequent treatment
evidence.explanation: SOLO1 provides direct long-term randomized evidence for maintenance olaparib in the BRCA-associated HGSOC facet.

treatments/2.description: Maintenance PARP inhibition provides durable clinical benefit after first-line platinum response in BRCA-associated HGSOC and is the clearest therapy linked to the BRCA-associated subtype facet represented in this entry. Olaparib carries the trial and regulatory evidence curated here; niraparib and rucaparib are the other approved maintenance agents in this setting.

evidence.snippet: The median progression-free survival was 10.3 months in the control group, 11.2 in the bevacizumab-initiation group, and 14.1 in the bevacizumab-throughout group.
evidence.explanation: The GOG-0218 primary endpoint result, quoted with all three arms so the benefit is attributable to continued maintenance rather than to bevacizumab during chemotherapy alone.

evidence.snippet: At the time of analysis, 76.3% of patients were alive, with no significant differences in overall survival among the three groups.
evidence.explanation: Records the negative overall-survival result, which is why this treatment is curated as a progression-free-survival benefit rather than a survival benefit.

evidence.snippet: progression-free survival (restricted mean) at 42 months was 22.4 months without bevacizumab versus 24.1 months with bevacizumab
evidence.explanation: The independent ICON7 confirmation, at a different bevacizumab dose and schedule.

evidence.snippet: An unfavorable KELIM score was associated with bevacizumab benefit compared with placebo (PFS: HR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59 to 0.82; OS: HR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.73 to 1.03)
evidence.explanation: GOG-0218 validates a clinically meaningful benefit signal for bevacizumab in a biomarker-defined subset of high-grade ovarian cancer.

treatments/3.description: Bevacizumab is used with chemotherapy and as maintenance therapy in advanced HGSOC, with the greatest observed benefit in patients whose tumors show poor intrinsic chemosensitivity.

evidence.snippet: the addition of HIPEC to interval cytoreductive surgery resulted in longer recurrence-free survival and overall survival than surgery alone and did not result in higher rates of side effects
evidence.explanation: OVHIPEC-1, a multicentre phase 3 randomised trial, is the primary clinical evidence for adding HIPEC to interval cytoreductive surgery in stage III epithelial ovarian cancer.

evidence.snippet: The median overall survival was 33.9 months in the surgery group and 45.7 months in the surgery-plus-HIPEC group.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the survival difference reported in the trial, supporting the effect size stated in the description.

evidence.snippet: the available data from two phase III trials seem to suggest that the addition of HIPEC to interval debulking surgery after neoadjuvant chemotherapy significantly improves PFS and OS. Conversely, HIPEC does not appear to offer any advantage after primary debulking surgery.
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the indication - the benefit is confined to the interval-debulking setting, so this supports the treatment only as scoped in its name and description.

treatments/4.description: Heated cisplatin perfused through the peritoneal cavity at the time of interval cytoreductive surgery, after neoadjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel. The rationale is compartmental: metastatic ovarian cancer sits on peritoneal surfaces that intravenous drug reaches poorly, so the drug is delivered into the compartment that carries the tumour burden. In the OVHIPEC-1 phase 3 trial the addition of HIPEC extended median overall survival from 33.9 to 45.7 months without increasing grade 3-4 toxicity. Benefit appears specific to the interval (post-neoadjuvant) setting; it has not been shown after primary debulking surgery, and the mechanism of benefit is not established.
