steps/8.description: Obesity-related insulin resistance travels with fatty liver, dyslipidaemia and low adiponectin. Insulin resistance from insulin-receptor dysfunction travels with none of them, and insulin resistance from AKT2 dysfunction phenocopies the obesity pattern. SHORT syndrome sits with the receptor group: four of five studied patients had extreme insulin resistance without dyslipidaemia or hepatic steatosis, and adiponectin was preserved in three of those four. Because PIK3R1 acts between the receptor and AKT, that placement is informative about where in the cascade the lesion sits, and it makes the metabolic profile a discriminating clinical feature rather than an incidental one.

evidence.snippet: In addition, mutant mice displayed defective insulin secretion and GLP-1 action on islets in vivo and in vitro.
evidence.explanation: The observation this node records, stated as a mouse result.

steps/9.description: A second, beta-cell arm of the metabolic phenotype, demonstrated only in the knock-in mouse: the mutation impairs insulin secretion and the action of GLP-1 on islets, in vivo and in vitro. If it holds in patients it means the diabetes is not purely a resistance phenomenon, which would matter for treatment choice. No equivalent human measurement is cited, so this node is model-derived throughout.

evidence.snippet: plays an important role in cell growth, proliferation, and survival
evidence.explanation: The pathway property the growth phenotype is attributed to. Cited as the basis for the inference, not as a measurement of growth-plate signalling.

evidence.snippet: the patients usually present a low birth weight and height, lipodystrophy, delayed bone age, hernias, low body mass index and a progeroid appearance
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the growth deficit is present from birth and is accompanied by delayed skeletal maturation, which is what makes it a growth-signalling phenotype rather than a nutritional one.

evidence.snippet: PI3K malfunction is associated with insulin resistance, decreased lipogenesis, increased energy expenditure, and possible IGF1 resistance.
evidence.explanation: Names three candidate routes to the growth phenotype that are more specific than "the pathway drives growth": IGF1 resistance, increased energy expenditure, and decreased lipogenesis. The review hedges on the IGF1 arm ("possible"), and that hedge is retained. Graded OTHER as a narrative review.

steps/10.description: Growth restriction in SHORT syndrome begins prenatally and continues after birth. It is attributed to downregulation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR axis, which drives cell growth and proliferation. This attribution rests on the pathway's known role rather than on a direct measurement in growth-plate tissue from patients.

evidence.snippet: The commonly observed clinical features of SHORT syndrome seen in the cohort included intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) <10th percentile, postnatal growth restriction, lipoatrophy and the characteristic facial gestalt.
evidence.explanation: "Commonly observed" in a 32-patient molecularly confirmed cohort. The source gives no percentage, so FREQUENT is the widest band consistent with the wording rather than a reported figure.

steps/11.description: Prenatal growth restriction, generally below the 10th percentile, and one of the features most consistently present in molecularly confirmed patients.

evidence.snippet: included intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) <10th percentile, postnatal growth restriction
evidence.explanation: Postnatal growth restriction listed among the commonly observed features.

steps/12.description: Postnatal growth restriction, continuous with the prenatal deficit; the "S" of the acronym.

evidence.snippet: postnatal growth restriction, lipoatrophy and the characteristic facial gestalt
evidence.explanation: Lipoatrophy among the commonly observed features of the confirmed cohort.

evidence.snippet: Lipodystrophy, characterized by selective loss of adipose tissue, is another typical feature of the syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Describes the nature of the fat loss.

steps/13.description: Partial lipodystrophy with selective loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue, predominantly of the face, chest and upper limbs, characteristically sparing the buttocks and legs; it contributes to the progeroid facial appearance.

evidence.snippet: Anterior chamber defects and insulin resistance or diabetes were also observed but were not as prevalent.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the feature and, explicitly, that it is less prevalent than the growth and lipoatrophy features. The band is set below those features on that basis rather than from a reported percentage.

steps/14.description: Severe post-receptor insulin resistance with compensatory hyperinsulinaemia, often detectable on oral glucose tolerance testing before fasting glucose becomes abnormal.

evidence.snippet: Severe insulin resistance may also lead to an early onset of type 2 diabetes, typically occurring in the second decade of life
evidence.explanation: Establishes diabetes as a consequence and gives its usual age of onset. The hedged "may" in the source is why the frequency band is conservative.

evidence.snippet: Given the high risk of diabetes mellitus, regular monitoring of glucose metabolism is warranted.
evidence.explanation: The cohort study's own risk assessment, which is what justifies surveillance.

steps/15.description: Diabetes arising from sustained severe insulin resistance, with onset typically in the second decade. The reported risk is high enough that the systematic cohort review recommends routine glucose monitoring.

evidence.snippet: Anterior chamber defects and insulin resistance or diabetes were also observed but were not as prevalent.
evidence.explanation: Anterior chamber defects present but explicitly less prevalent than the core growth and adipose features.

evidence.snippet: short stature, progeroid face, and Rieger anomaly (SHORT syndrome)
evidence.explanation: Rieger anomaly as a defining feature in the families in which the hotspot variant was identified.

steps/16.description: Anterior segment dysgenesis of the Axenfeld-Rieger type; the "R" of the acronym. Associated anterior chamber findings include posterior embryotoxon and glaucoma.

evidence.snippet: ophthalmic anomalies (Rieger anomaly, posterior embryotoxon, glaucoma)
evidence.explanation: Names glaucoma among the ophthalmic features. No frequency is recorded because none of the cited sources gives one.

steps/17.description: Raised intraocular pressure and glaucoma, a recognised consequence of the anterior chamber dysgenesis and the reason ophthalmological assessment is recommended.

evidence.snippet: ophthalmic anomalies (Rieger anomaly, posterior embryotoxon, glaucoma)
evidence.explanation: Names posterior embryotoxon among the ophthalmic features.

steps/18.description: A prominent, anteriorly displaced Schwalbe line, part of the anterior segment phenotype.

evidence.snippet: short stature, hyperextensibility of joints, hernias, ocular depression
evidence.explanation: Ocular depression as a defining acronym feature.

steps/19.description: Ocular depression, the "O" of the acronym, and part of the characteristic facial gestalt.

evidence.snippet: a characteristic facial gestalt (e.g. triangular face with a small thin, thin lip, downturned mouth, low-set posteriorly rotated ears, prominent forehead, underdeveloped or thin nasal alae as well as wrinkles)
evidence.explanation: Spells out the components of the facial gestalt, of which the triangular face is the bindable element.

evidence.snippet: lipoatrophy and the characteristic facial gestalt
evidence.explanation: The facial gestalt among the commonly observed features of the confirmed cohort.

steps/20.description: Part of the characteristic facial gestalt, together with a small chin, thin lips, a downturned mouth and low-set posteriorly rotated ears. The gestalt is one of the features most consistently present in molecularly confirmed patients.

evidence.snippet: The less specific, or minor features of SHORT syndrome include teething delay, thin wrinkled skin, speech delay, sensorineural deafness, hyperextensibility of joints and inguinal hernia.
evidence.explanation: Places teething delay among the minor features. No frequency band is recorded because the source grades specificity, not prevalence.

steps/21.description: Teething delay, the "T" of the acronym; classified by the cohort review as one of the less specific, minor features.

evidence.snippet: almost all postpubertal women affected present polycystic ovary syndrome
evidence.explanation: "Almost all" is the basis for the VERY_FREQUENT band, which applies to the postpubertal female subgroup rather than to all patients.

steps/22.description: Polycystic ovary syndrome in postpubertal affected women, attributed to hyperinsulinaemia secondary to the insulin resistance.

evidence.snippet: Facial dysmorphism including ocular depression, triangular shaped face, frontal bossing, large low-set ears, and micrognathia were the most consistent features followed by lipodystrophy, insulin resistance, and intrauterine growth restriction.
evidence.explanation: Places frontal bossing within the most consistent feature group, and gives the ordering that the frequency bands in this entry follow.

steps/23.description: A prominent forehead, part of the progeroid craniofacial gestalt that the systematic review found to be the most consistent feature of the syndrome.

evidence.snippet: triangular shaped face, frontal bossing, large low-set ears, and micrognathia were the most consistent features
evidence.explanation: Micrognathia among the most consistent features.

steps/24.description: Mandibular retrognathia, a skeletal rather than adipose component of the facial gestalt.

evidence.snippet: frontal bossing, large low-set ears, and micrognathia were the most consistent features
evidence.explanation: Large low-set ears among the most consistent features.

steps/25.description: Large, low-set ears, part of the facial gestalt.

evidence.snippet: Individuals have a distinct progeroid craniofacial appearance with a triangular face, frontal bossing, hypoplastic or thin alae nasi, large low-set ears, and mandibular retrognathia.
evidence.explanation: Names the components of the progeroid craniofacial appearance, including the alae nasi.

steps/26.description: Hypoplastic or thin alae nasi, a recurrent component of the progeroid craniofacial appearance.

evidence.snippet: Teething delay, microdontia, hypodontia, and enamel hypoplasia have all been reported.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the wider dental phenotype. The source says "have all been reported" without frequencies, so no band is recorded.

steps/27.description: Reduced tooth number, one of the dental findings the systematic appraisal set out to characterise. The dental phenotype of this syndrome is broader than the acronym's "teething delay" implies.

evidence.snippet: Teething delay, microdontia, hypodontia, and enamel hypoplasia have all been reported.
evidence.explanation: Microdontia among the reported dental findings.

steps/28.description: Small teeth, reported alongside the hypodontia and enamel defects.

evidence.snippet: microdontia, hypodontia, and enamel hypoplasia have all been reported
evidence.explanation: Enamel hypoplasia among the reported dental findings.

steps/29.description: Defective enamel formation, completing the dental phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Four of 5 patients had extreme insulin resistance without dyslipidemia or hepatic steatosis.
evidence.explanation: Directly contradicts the presence of hepatic steatosis in four of five studied patients, which is why this item is graded REFUTE rather than SUPPORT.

steps/30.description: Characteristically ABSENT. This entry records the phenotype in order to record its absence, because that absence is diagnostically useful: extreme insulin resistance without fatty liver points away from obesity-related insulin resistance and towards a proximal receptor-to-PI3K lesion. Recorded with REFUTE evidence rather than omitted, so that a query for "does this disease cause fatty liver" gets an answer rather than silence.

evidence.snippet: Four of 5 patients had extreme insulin resistance without dyslipidemia or hepatic steatosis.
evidence.explanation: Contradicts the presence of dyslipidaemia in four of five studied patients. The binding is to the hypertriglyceridaemia term because that is the specific lipid abnormality the obesity-related pattern would predict.

steps/31.description: Characteristically ABSENT, for the same reason as the hepatic steatosis and recorded the same way.

evidence.snippet: Both human subjects had Rieger anomaly with similar defects including thin irides and irregular pupils
evidence.explanation: Thin irides in both human subjects carrying the hotspot allele. Two patients, so no frequency band is recorded.

steps/32.description: Thin iris stroma. Directly measured by OCT in the knock-in mouse and observed in human R649W carriers, it is the most precisely characterised component of the anterior segment phenotype and the only one with a quantitative animal readout.

evidence.snippet: thin irides and irregular pupils, as well as a prominent ring of Schwalbe
evidence.explanation: Irregular pupils in the human subjects, alongside the posterior embryotoxon this entry already curates as the prominent Schwalbe ring.

steps/33.description: Irregular and enlarged pupil, secondary to the iris hypoplasia.

evidence.snippet: as well as a prominent ring of Schwalbe, goniosynechiae, early cataract formation, and glaucoma
evidence.explanation: Goniosynechiae in both human subjects, reported together with the glaucoma.

steps/34.description: Goniosynechiae. Clinically important because adhesions across the iridocorneal angle obstruct aqueous outflow, which is the route from anterior segment dysgenesis to the glaucoma this entry also curates.

evidence.snippet: goniosynechiae, early cataract formation, and glaucoma
evidence.explanation: Early cataract in the two human subjects.

steps/35.description: Early cataract formation, reported in both human R649W subjects examined ophthalmologically.

evidence.snippet: This mutation led to impaired interaction between p85α and IRS-1 and reduced AKT-mediated insulin signaling in fibroblasts from affected subjects
evidence.explanation: Directly links the hotspot variant to loss of the p85-alpha/IRS-1 interaction.

edges/1.description: The variant SH2 domain is the surface through which p85-alpha docks onto tyrosine-phosphorylated IRS-1, so a change in this domain acts directly on that interaction.

evidence.snippet: Functional studies on lymphoblastoid cells with the PIK3R1 c.1906_1907insC mutation showed decreased phosphorylation of the downstream S6 target of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway.
evidence.explanation: Measures the downstream consequence in patient-derived cells.

edges/2.description: Failure to recruit the holoenzyme to IRS-1 is the immediate cause of reduced downstream AKT and S6 phosphorylation.

evidence.snippet: Functional data from fibroblasts derived from individuals with PIK3R1 mutations showed severe insulin resistance for both proximal and distal PI3K-dependent signaling.
evidence.explanation: Shows the signalling defect is present at both proximal and distal levels of the cascade in patient cells.

edges/3.description: Reduced PI3K-dependent signalling downstream of an intact insulin receptor is what post-receptor insulin resistance consists of at the cellular level.

evidence.snippet: Normal PI3K activity is critical for adipose differentiation and insulin signaling
evidence.explanation: States the dependency of adipose differentiation on PI3K activity that this edge asserts.

edges/4.description: PI3K activity is required for adipose differentiation, so the same reduction in signalling that impairs insulin action also constrains adipogenesis.

evidence.snippet: These data demonstrate the ability of this heterozygous mutation to alter PI3K activity in vivo and the central role of PI3K in insulin/growth factor action, adipocyte function, and glucose metabolism.
evidence.explanation: Places the secretory defect within the same in vivo PI3K lesion. The islet mechanism itself is not resolved, hence unknown intermediates.

edges/5.description: PI3K signalling operates in the beta cell as well as in insulin target tissues, so the secretory defect seen in the knock-in mouse plausibly shares this upstream lesion. The intervening steps in the islet are not established.

evidence.snippet: Facial dysmorphism including ocular depression, triangular shaped face, frontal bossing, large low-set ears, and micrognathia were the most consistent features
evidence.explanation: Establishes the craniofacial gestalt as the most consistent element of the syndrome, which is what makes it worth a node despite the missing mechanism.

edges/6.description: The craniofacial and dental features segregate with PIK3R1 variants and are, on systematic appraisal, the most consistent part of the phenotype. No developmental mechanism connecting reduced PI3K signalling to them is established, so the edge is drawn with unknown intermediates rather than omitted.

evidence.snippet: in two unrelated families affected by partial lipodystrophy, low body mass index, short stature, progeroid face, and Rieger anomaly (SHORT syndrome)
evidence.explanation: Rieger anomaly segregates with the same variant as the metabolic and growth features, which is the basis for placing it downstream of the shared signalling lesion. It is co-segregation, not a demonstrated developmental mechanism.

edges/7.description: The anterior chamber phenotype is attributed to the same signalling defect because it segregates with PIK3R1 variants, but no developmental route from reduced PI3K signalling to neural-crest-derived anterior segment formation is established. The edge is drawn with unknown intermediates rather than left disconnected, because leaving it disconnected would imply an independent cause the evidence does not support.

evidence.snippet: PIK3R1 is involved in the phosphatidylinositol 3 kinase (PI3K) signaling cascade and, as such, plays an important role in cell growth, proliferation, and survival.
evidence.explanation: The authors' statement of the pathway's growth role, which is the basis for attributing the growth restriction to pathway downregulation. This is an inference about the pathway rather than a measurement in growth plate tissue.

edges/8.description: The PI3K-AKT-mTOR axis drives cell growth and proliferation, so its downregulation is the proposed route from the variant to the growth phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Our findings extend the genetic causes of severe insulin-resistance syndromes
evidence.explanation: Places SHORT syndrome among the severe insulin-resistance syndromes.

edges/9.description: The cellular signalling defect is the mechanism of the clinical insulin resistance.

evidence.snippet: Severe insulin resistance may also lead to an early onset of type 2 diabetes, typically occurring in the second decade of life
evidence.explanation: States both the causal step and its usual timing.

edges/10.description: Sustained severe insulin resistance is the route to diabetes in this disorder.

evidence.snippet: Four of 5 patients had extreme insulin resistance without dyslipidemia or hepatic steatosis.
evidence.explanation: The counted observation that defines this node.

edges/11.description: The insulin resistance of SHORT syndrome does not carry the metabolic company it usually keeps. This is not an absence of findings but a positive, discriminating feature.

evidence.snippet: almost all postpubertal women affected present polycystic ovary syndrome
evidence.explanation: Records the near-universal ovarian phenotype in postpubertal affected women. The quote establishes the association; the insulin-mediated mechanism is the curator's inference and is why this edge is marked INDIRECT.

edges/12.description: Hyperinsulinaemia secondary to insulin resistance is the conventional route to the ovarian phenotype; the cited source reports the association, not the intervening steps.

evidence.snippet: Four of 5 patients had extreme insulin resistance without dyslipidemia or hepatic steatosis.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the absence of dyslipidaemia, which is the claim the linked phenotype records.

edges/13.description: The other half of the dissociation, and recorded the same way: an expected feature that is characteristically absent.

evidence.snippet: Four of 5 patients had extreme insulin resistance without dyslipidemia or hepatic steatosis.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the absence, which is the claim the linked phenotype records.

edges/14.description: Recorded as an expected feature that is characteristically absent. The phenotype entry carries REFUTE evidence rather than asserting its presence.

evidence.snippet: mutant mice displayed defective insulin secretion and GLP-1 action on islets in vivo and in vitro
evidence.explanation: The secretory and incretin defect in the knock-in model.

edges/15.description: A secretory defect on top of resistance would lower the threshold for overt hyperglycaemia. Marked indirect because the secretory defect is shown in mouse and the diabetes is a human phenotype.

evidence.snippet: causing an aged appearance of the patients suffering from the SHORT syndrome
evidence.explanation: States the causal contribution of the facial fat loss to the appearance. The skeletal components of the gestalt are not covered by this edge.

edges/16.description: Facial lipoatrophy is a major contributor to the progeroid facial gestalt. It is not the whole of it - frontal bossing and micrognathia are skeletal - but the loss of facial fat is what gives the aged appearance.

evidence.snippet: Lipodystrophy, characterized by selective loss of adipose tissue, is another typical feature of the syndrome. It is displayed mainly in the face
evidence.explanation: Establishes facial adipose loss. The specific attribution of ocular depression to periorbital fat loss is the curator's reading, which is why the edge is indirect.

edges/17.description: Loss of periorbital fat contributes to the ocular depression that gives the acronym its "O".

evidence.snippet: It is displayed mainly in the face, chest and upper extremities, often sparing the buttocks and legs
evidence.explanation: The regional distribution of the fat loss, which is what makes it partial rather than generalised.

edges/18.description: Failure of adipose differentiation produces the regional loss of subcutaneous fat that defines the lipodystrophy.

evidence.snippet: The commonly observed clinical features of SHORT syndrome seen in the cohort included intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR)
evidence.explanation: Establishes IUGR as one of the consistently observed features in the molecularly confirmed cohort.

edges/19.description: The prenatal arm of the growth phenotype.

evidence.snippet: postnatal growth restriction, lipoatrophy and the characteristic facial gestalt
evidence.explanation: Lists postnatal growth restriction among the consistently observed features.

edges/20.description: The postnatal arm of the same growth phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Individuals have a distinct progeroid craniofacial appearance with a triangular face, frontal bossing, hypoplastic or thin alae nasi, large low-set ears, and mandibular retrognathia.
evidence.explanation: Names frontal bossing as a component of the craniofacial appearance.

edges/21.description: A skeletal component of the gestalt.

evidence.snippet: a triangular face, frontal bossing, hypoplastic or thin alae nasi, large low-set ears, and mandibular retrognathia
evidence.explanation: Names mandibular retrognathia as a component.

edges/22.description: Mandibular retrognathia, a skeletal component of the gestalt.

evidence.snippet: hypoplastic or thin alae nasi, large low-set ears, and mandibular retrognathia
evidence.explanation: Names the ear finding as a component.

edges/23.description: Large low-set ears, a component of the gestalt.

evidence.snippet: a triangular face, frontal bossing, hypoplastic or thin alae nasi
evidence.explanation: Names the alae nasi finding as a component.

evidence.snippet: Teething delay, microdontia, hypodontia, and enamel hypoplasia have all been reported.
evidence.explanation: Groups the teething delay with the wider dental phenotype.

edges/25.description: The "T" of the acronym, part of the dental phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Teething delay, microdontia, hypodontia, and enamel hypoplasia have all been reported.
evidence.explanation: Hypodontia among the reported dental findings.

evidence.snippet: microdontia, hypodontia, and enamel hypoplasia have all been reported
evidence.explanation: Microdontia among the reported dental findings.

evidence.snippet: hypodontia, and enamel hypoplasia have all been reported
evidence.explanation: Enamel hypoplasia among the reported dental findings.

evidence.snippet: ophthalmic anomalies (Rieger anomaly, posterior embryotoxon, glaucoma)
evidence.explanation: Groups glaucoma with the other anterior segment findings as one ophthalmic phenotype.

edges/29.description: Raised intraocular pressure follows from maldevelopment of the drainage structures of the anterior chamber.

evidence.snippet: ophthalmic anomalies (Rieger anomaly, posterior embryotoxon, glaucoma)
evidence.explanation: Posterior embryotoxon among the anterior segment findings.

edges/30.description: An anteriorly displaced Schwalbe line is part of the same anterior segment maldevelopment.

evidence.snippet: Both human subjects had Rieger anomaly with similar defects including thin irides and irregular pupils
evidence.explanation: The thin iris in human R649W carriers, matching the mouse finding.

edges/31.description: Thinning of the iris stroma, the component of the anterior segment phenotype that the knock-in mouse reproduces and that is measurable by OCT.

evidence.snippet: Both human subjects had Rieger anomaly with similar defects including thin irides and irregular pupils
evidence.explanation: Irregular pupils in human carriers. The mouse data in the same paper make the dependence on iris thinning explicit, which is why the link is indirect.

edges/32.description: The irregular, enlarged pupil follows from the iris hypoplasia rather than being an independent defect.

evidence.snippet: as well as a prominent ring of Schwalbe, goniosynechiae, early cataract formation, and glaucoma
evidence.explanation: The additional human anterior segment findings, which include the angle adhesions.

edges/33.description: Goniosynechiae, adhesions across the iridocorneal angle. Present in the human subjects and absent from the mouse, which is part of why the model is graded as reproducing the iris defect rather than the whole anterior segment phenotype.

evidence.snippet: goniosynechiae, early cataract formation, and glaucoma
evidence.explanation: Early cataract in both human R649W subjects.

edges/34.description: Early cataract in the human subjects. Whether it is a direct consequence of the anterior segment maldevelopment or secondary to the glaucoma and its treatment is not addressed by the source.

evidence.snippet: ophthalmic anomalies (Rieger anomaly, posterior embryotoxon, glaucoma)
evidence.explanation: Names the anterior segment findings that characterise the syndrome.

edges/35.description: Anterior segment maldevelopment is what the Rieger anomaly consists of.

evidence.snippet: Heterozygous mutations in exon 14 of PIK3R1 were subsequently identified by Sanger sequencing in three additional affected individuals and two affected family members.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the exon 14 clustering across multiple affected individuals.

evidence.snippet: The other mutation, a de novo truncating mutation
evidence.explanation: A truncating allele in the same region, showing the spectrum is not restricted to missense changes.

evidence.snippet: Eight of these families had a recurrent missense mutation (c.1945C>T; p.Arg649Trp).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the recurrence of the hotspot allele across reported families.

evidence.snippet: Sequencing result indicated c.1960C > T of PIK3R1 gene a novel nonsense mutation, leading to the termination of protein translation
evidence.explanation: An additional nonsense allele in the same region.

genes/0.notes: Reported alleles are heterozygous and cluster in exon 14, encoding the C-terminal SH2 domain of p85-alpha; they include missense (recurrently c.1945C>T, p.Arg649Trp), frameshift (c.1906_1907insC, p.Asn636Thrfs*18) and nonsense (c.1971T>G, p.Tyr657*; c.1960C>T, p.Gln654*) changes. The domain clustering is the clinically load-bearing observation: variants elsewhere in the same gene, notably splice-site changes affecting the inter-SH2 region, cause activated PI3K-delta syndrome 2 instead, which has the opposite effect on PI3K signalling. This entry does not assign a `functional_impact_category`: the reported functional data establish that pathway signalling is reduced, but none of the cited sources distinguishes haploinsufficiency from a dominant-negative action of the mutant subunit, and the recurrent missense hotspot in a heterozygous state is compatible with either.

evidence.snippet: She was treated with metformin and canagliflozin (a sodium glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor), which ameliorated overt diurnal hyperglycemia and mild nocturnal hypoglycemia and reduced her blood HbA1c around 7%.
evidence.explanation: The regimen and its measured effect in the one reported case. A single case, which is why this is recorded as reported practice rather than as established therapy.

evidence.snippet: a usefulness of SGLT2 inhibitor in the treatment of IRDM
evidence.explanation: The authors' own conclusion about the drug class.

treatments/0.description: Once diabetes is overt, the reported regimen is an insulin sensitiser plus an insulin-independent glucose-lowering agent. In the documented case, metformin with canagliflozin brought HbA1c from 9.2% to around 7% and, notably, corrected both the daytime hyperglycaemia and the nocturnal hypoglycaemia. The rationale for an SGLT2 inhibitor here is mechanistic as well as empirical: it lowers glucose by a renal route that does not depend on the impaired PI3K arm of insulin signalling.

evidence.snippet: The patient's blood glucose levels improved significantly, with HbA1c decreased from 14% to 8.8% within 6 months of starting the multi-agent regimen
evidence.explanation: The measured response, with its timescale. A single case.

evidence.snippet: Currently, there are no established guidelines for the treatment of diabetes in SHORT syndrome patients.
evidence.explanation: States the evidence base this and every other treatment entry here rests on: case reports, not guidelines.

evidence.snippet: our treatment plans, including lifestyle intervention combined with metformin and pioglitazone, were carried out for this patient. After the intervention, insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia in this patient were significantly decreased during a 6-month follow up
evidence.explanation: An independent case using a metformin plus thiazolidinedione combination, with the same direction of response over the same interval.

evidence.snippet: we implemented a comprehensive treatment plan, including lifestyle interventions, metformin, and voglibose for glucose control. After 6 months of continuous observation, the patient's blood glucose levels and insulin resistance improved significantly.
evidence.explanation: A third independent case, in a patient carrying the same c.1945C>T hotspot allele this entry curates, using metformin with an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor.

evidence.snippet: We report two Chinese girls with SHORT syndrome who presented with growth retardation, dysmorphic features, insulin resistance, and diabetes.
evidence.explanation: Two further patients in whom metformin was the chosen agent. Cited as part of the case series behind metformin being the consistent first agent across every published report, which is the only sense in which this literature supports a first-line choice.

treatments/1.description: Where a single agent is not enough, published practice is to stack oral agents with complementary mechanisms rather than move to insulin - which matters here, because insulin resistance of this severity makes injected insulin both unattractive and only partly effective. In the reported case, metformin, an SGLT-2 inhibitor, a sulfonylurea, a thiazolidinedione and a GLP-1 agonist together took HbA1c from 14% to 8.8% in six months and then to 7.4%, and deferred insulin. Two of those classes are worth identifying separately: the SGLT-2 inhibitor lowers glucose by a renal route that does not depend on the impaired PI3K arm at all, and the GLP-1 agonist acts on the incretin axis that the knock-in mouse shows to be defective in this disease.

evidence.snippet: By utilizing a combination of oral anti-glycemic agents with complementary mechanisms of action (metformin, sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones, and GLP-1 agonists), insulin therapy was delayed.
evidence.explanation: Names the GLP-1 agonist among the agents used. That an incretin-directed drug is used in a disease with a documented incretin defect is the reason for this link; the source does not isolate its contribution.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: A GLP-1 agonist acts directly on the incretin axis this pathograph records as defective. The link is mechanistically motivated rather than demonstrated: the incretin defect is a mouse finding, and the case report does not attribute the patient's response to any one agent in the combination.

evidence.snippet: GH dosage was increased from 0.23 to 0.36 mg/kg/week, but statural response to GH therapy remained poor.
evidence.explanation: The growth outcome, which is the clearest argument against the intervention in this disorder.

evidence.snippet: These findings imply a critical role of pubertal development and/or advanced age rather than GH therapy in the development of IRDM
evidence.explanation: Graded REFUTE because it contradicts the claim this treatment entry might otherwise be read as making - that growth hormone causes the diabetes. The authors attribute the diabetes to puberty instead.

treatments/2.description: Long treated as contraindicated because growth hormone is diabetogenic and these patients are already severely insulin resistant. The reported evidence complicates that: growth response was poor in the one documented case, and the literature review in the same paper found insulin-resistant diabetes in 10 of 15 untreated patients aged 12 or over and in none of three treated or six untreated patients aged 10 or under - an age effect, not a treatment effect. So the case against growth hormone here rests on lack of benefit more securely than on causing the diabetes.

evidence.snippet: Given the high risk of diabetes mellitus, regular monitoring of glucose metabolism is warranted.
evidence.explanation: The explicit management recommendation from the cohort review.

treatments/3.description: There is no disease-modifying therapy. Management centres on surveillance for and treatment of the metabolic consequences: because the risk of diabetes is high, regular monitoring of glucose metabolism is recommended, with treatment of hyperglycaemia when it develops.

evidence.snippet: An echocardiogram, ophthalmological and hearing assessments are also recommended.
evidence.explanation: The surveillance recommendation this treatment entry implements.

treatments/4.description: Cardiac, ophthalmological and audiological assessment are recommended alongside the metabolic monitoring, reflecting the cardiac, anterior chamber and sensorineural components of the phenotype.

evidence.snippet: 47 patients with APDS2 have been reported to date, only one of them sharing both PIK3R1-related phenotypes.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies how exceptional the overlap was thought to be before this report.

evidence.snippet: Here we describe two more patients affected by APDS2 and SHORT syndrome, which highlights that this association may not be so infrequent.
evidence.explanation: The observation that reopens the question: the overlap is more common than the single prior case suggested.

evidence.snippet: This pathogenic variant had been previously associated with APDS2; however, it had not been associated with SHORT syndrome. The exact mechanisms linking both conditions are yet to be identified.
evidence.explanation: The sharpest form of the problem: one splice allele, previously an APDS2 allele, producing SHORT syndrome features in this patient. Cited here because it is the strongest published case against the split this entry maintains, and the authors state plainly that the mechanism is unknown.

evidence.snippet: LOF variants in an intronic splice site (c.1425+1G.C/A/T) in the PI3KR1 gene have been identified in patients affected with both APDS2 and SHORT syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the specific intronic splice site where the overlap alleles cluster, which is what makes the overlap look like a property of a variant class rather than a coincidence.

open_questions/0.rationale: The two PIK3R1 diseases are usually described as having opposite effects on the pathway, which makes their co-occurrence in one individual mechanistically awkward rather than merely unusual. Reported overlap cases show it is not a theoretical concern: two further patients with both phenotypes were described in 2017, taking the total beyond the single previously known case, and the authors concluded the association may not be rare. Resolving this matters for curation because it determines whether the two entries can keep independent pathographs or whether a shared allele-to-phenotype model is needed.

evidence.snippet: PIK3R1 C-terminal mutations impair insulin signaling only in some cellular contexts
evidence.explanation: The authors' explicit statement of context-dependence, which is what this question is about.

evidence.snippet: showed severely reduced insulin-stimulated association of mutant but not WT p85α with IRS1, but normal downstream signaling
evidence.explanation: A measured case where the binding defect did not propagate downstream. This is the single most direct challenge to the simple linear reading of the pathograph, and is recorded here rather than omitted because it is inconvenient.

open_questions/1.rationale: The pathograph in this entry routes everything through one node in which PI3K-AKT signalling is reduced, and that is how the founding papers framed it. The 2016 study that established the dyslipidaemia dissociation complicates the picture in two ways. First, it states outright that these mutations impair insulin signalling only in some cellular contexts. Second, in cells from one patient carrying the p.Tyr657X allele, the mutant p85-alpha failed to associate with IRS1 while downstream signalling was normal - a binding defect that did not propagate. Taken together these say the lesion is not a uniform dial turned down across every tissue, which is what the single node implies. The tissue selectivity would also explain the dissociation directly: hepatic lipogenesis is spared while glucose disposal is not. Nothing cited here identifies what makes a given cell type sensitive or resistant, so the node is kept as one and this question records the qualification rather than splitting the pathograph on speculation.

evidence.snippet: A dominant-negative mutation in the p85α regulatory subunit of PI3K affects development of the iris, and contributes to changes consistent with anterior segment dysgenesis in both humans and mice.
evidence.explanation: Establishes sufficiency, which is the half of the question that is answered.

evidence.snippet: While overall eye development was normal with clear cornea and lens, normal anterior chamber volume, normal intraocular pressure, and no changes in the retinal structure, OCT images of the knock-in mouse eyes revealed a significant decrease in thickness and width of the iris
evidence.explanation: The selectivity of the mouse phenotype - iris only, everything else normal - which is the observation any mechanistic account would have to explain and none does.

open_questions/2.rationale: The gap here is narrower than it looks, and narrower than an earlier draft of this entry claimed. Sufficiency is established: the heterozygous R649W allele produces iris hypoplasia with an enlarged irregular pupil in the knock-in mouse, and the same allele produces Rieger anomaly in human carriers, so the p85-alpha lesion demonstrably reaches anterior segment development in vivo. What is missing is everything between. The anterior segment derives from periocular neural crest, and no cited source identifies which crest population, which developmental window, or which PI3K-dependent process is affected - nor why the mouse stops at the iris while humans go on to goniosynechiae, cataract and glaucoma. That species difference is itself a clue nobody has followed up. The pathophysiology node is connected to the upstream signalling node with unknown intermediates, which is the honest encoding of "we know it gets there, we do not know how".

evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis of aggrecan complementary DNA from an affected individual revealed homozygosity for a missense mutation (c.6799G --> A) that predicts a p.D2267N amino acid substitution in the C-type lectin domain within the G3 domain of aggrecan.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the causal variant and its precise position within the protein, which is what the rest of the pathograph depends on.

evidence.snippet: The D2267 residue is predicted to coordinate binding of a calcium ion, which influences the conformational binding loops of the C-type lectin domain that mediate interactions with tenascins and other extracellular-matrix proteins.
evidence.explanation: Gives the structural reason the substitution should affect binding rather than abundance, which is the hypothesis the next node tests. Graded COMPUTATIONAL because the quoted sentence reports a structural prediction about the residue, not a measurement; the measurement that tests it is the surface plasmon resonance result carried by the binding node.

evidence.snippet: In contrast, the present individuals had heterozygous mutations in the CS1 and CS2 domains, consisting of a large number of repeats.
evidence.explanation: Places the second family's variants outside the lectin domain, which is why this node is named for ACAN rather than for a CLD lesion.

steps/1.description: The two reported families carry variants in different parts of the protein, and the node is named generically so it does not assert one lesion for both. The founding family is homozygous for c.6799G>A, predicting p.D2267N in the C-type lectin domain of aggrecan's G3 domain; that identification constrains what kind of mechanism this is, since the locus was mapped by identity-by-descent to a 17.4 Mb interval containing 296 genes and ranking those genes by cartilage-selective expression left only two, of which ACAN was one. The substituted residue is predicted to coordinate a calcium ion that shapes the binding loops of the lectin domain, and it is this allele that carries the functional work downstream. The second patient instead carries two missense variants in the chondroitin sulfate CS1 and CS2 domains, assessed only in silico. The mechanistic arms below are established for the lectin-domain allele; what the CS-domain variants do is not known.

evidence.snippet: Expression of the normal and mutant G3 domains in mammalian cells showed that the mutation created a functional N-glycosylation site but did not adversely affect protein trafficking and secretion.
evidence.explanation: Directly excludes a secretion or trafficking defect, which is what makes this node a genuine constraint on the mechanism rather than a detail.

steps/2.description: A negative result, and a load-bearing one. Expressing normal and mutant G3 domains in mammalian cells showed the mutation created a new functional N-glycosylation site but did not impair trafficking or secretion. That rules out the mechanisms this disease would otherwise be assumed to have - haploinsufficiency, retention in the endoplasmic reticulum, degradation of a misfolded product - and forces the mechanism onto what the secreted protein then fails to do.

evidence.snippet: Surface-plasmon-resonance studies showed that the mutation influenced the binding and kinetics of the interactions between the aggrecan G3 domain and tenascin-C.
evidence.explanation: The direct biophysical measurement of the binding defect, on the specific interaction this node names.

steps/3.description: The functional lesion. Surface plasmon resonance showed the substitution changes both the affinity and the kinetics of the interaction between the aggrecan G3 domain and tenascin-C. The G3 lectin domain is how aggrecan engages the wider matrix network - tenascin-R and tenascin-C, fibulins, fibrillin-1 - all in a calcium-dependent manner, so a change at the calcium-coordinating residue degrades the anchoring rather than the molecule.

evidence.snippet: Aggrecan provides the hydrated gel structure important for the load-bearing properties of joints and plays a key role in cartilage and bone morphogenesis.
evidence.explanation: States aggrecan's structural role in the matrix, which is the function this node asserts is degraded. Graded OTHER because the source is a narrative review rather than a primary study.

steps/4.description: Aggrecan is the major proteoglycan of growth-plate and articular cartilage and provides the hydrated gel that gives the tissue its load-bearing properties. Degrading how it is anchored degrades the matrix as a mechanical structure, which is the level at which a molecular binding defect becomes a tissue phenotype.

evidence.snippet: These findings identify an autosomal-recessive skeletal dysplasia and a significant role for the aggrecan C-type lectin domain in regulating endochondral ossification and, thereby, height.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own causal statement linking the lectin domain through endochondral ossification to stature, which is exactly the step this node represents.

evidence.snippet: Linear bone growth is determined by the division and growth of matrix-producing chondrocytes at the growth plate.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the growth plate as the site where matrix quality translates into stature. Graded OTHER as a review.

steps/5.description: Linear bone growth is produced by chondrocyte division and matrix production at the growth plate, then replacement of that cartilage by bone. A defective matrix compromises both the template and the mechanical environment the chondrocytes work in. Because the vertebral bodies, epiphyses and metaphyses are all sites of endochondral growth, one lesion at this node produces the combined spondylar, epiphyseal and metaphyseal picture the disease is named for - which is why this is a single dysplasia rather than three coincident ones.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of a nuclear family with three affected offspring identified an autosomal-recessive form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia characterized by severe short stature and a unique constellation of radiographic findings.
evidence.explanation: Establishes severe short stature as the defining clinical feature in the original family.

evidence.snippet: At our first examination, his height was 118.3 cm (−9.1 SD), his weight was 38.9 kg (−2.3 SD)
evidence.explanation: Gives the measured stature in the second reported patient, which is the basis for describing the severity range rather than a single figure.

steps/6.description: Disproportionate and micromelic, with acromesomelic limb shortening. The severity differs sharply between the two reported families: 66-71 cm in the three original siblings, against 118.3 cm (-9.1 SD) in the second patient. Both are severe, but they are not the same disease severity, and the entry does not average them.

evidence.snippet: He showed acromesomelic shortening of the limbs and relative macrocephaly.
evidence.explanation: Records the limb-shortening pattern that makes the stature disproportionate rather than uniformly reduced.

steps/7.description: The proportion is micromelic despite the spondylar involvement, with acromesomelic shortening of the limbs. That combination is part of what distinguishes this dysplasia radiographically.

evidence.snippet: The spine showed moderate platyspondyly with cervical lordosis and thoracolumbar kyphosis.
evidence.explanation: Records platyspondyly and the associated spinal curvature in the second patient.

steps/8.description: Moderate, with rectangular vertebral bodies and irregular endplates. It is the spondylar component of the spondylo-epi-metaphyseal triad.

evidence.snippet: The long bones were short and relatively broad, with metaphyseal flaring.
evidence.explanation: Describes the metaphyseal abnormality directly.

steps/9.description: Metaphyseal flaring of short, relatively broad long bones - the metaphyseal component of the triad, and one of the radiological hallmarks reported in the original family.

evidence.snippet: The radiological hallmarks included moderate platyspondyly with rectangular vertebral bodies, wide metaphyses and small, irregular epiphyses, multiple clefts of the cervical spine, and bradydactyly with accessory carpal ossification centers.
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the radiological hallmarks including the epiphyseal abnormality. The typographical error in "bradydactyly" is present in the source and is preserved so the quote stays exact.

steps/10.description: Small, irregular epiphyses of the long bones - the epiphyseal component, reported as a radiological hallmark of the original family.

evidence.snippet: Brachydactyly was very severe, with short, broad thumbs, horizontal nails, and telescoping interphalangeal joints.
evidence.explanation: Describes the hand phenotype in the original family in the detail that makes it distinctive.

steps/11.description: Severe in the original family, with short broad thumbs, horizontal nails, telescoping interphalangeal joints and accessory carpal ossification centres; generalized but less extreme in the second patient.

evidence.snippet: He showed acromesomelic shortening of the limbs and relative macrocephaly.
evidence.explanation: Records relative macrocephaly in the second patient.

steps/12.description: Present in both reports, and relative rather than absolute - the head is normally grown while the rest of the skeleton is not, which is what the growth-plate localisation of the defect predicts.

evidence.snippet: craniofacial abnormalities (relative macrocephaly, severe midface hypoplasia with absent nasal cartilage, relative prognathism, and low-set, posteriorly rotated ears)
evidence.explanation: The positive finding in the original family, which is what puts this feature in three of the four reported patients.

evidence.snippet: He had no midface hypoplasia, prognathism, or low-set ears.
evidence.explanation: A negative finding in the second patient, quoted because it is what establishes the craniofacial features as variable rather than defining. Marked REFUTE against the claim that this feature is part of the syndrome in every patient; it is the reason the frequency is FREQUENT and not OBLIGATE.

steps/13.description: Severe, with absent nasal cartilage, in all three siblings of the original family. Notably absent in the second patient, whose face was described as normal - so the craniofacial component is not an obligate part of the syndrome, but it is present in three of the four reported patients.

evidence.snippet: craniofacial abnormalities (relative macrocephaly, severe midface hypoplasia with absent nasal cartilage, relative prognathism, and low-set, posteriorly rotated ears) as well as a short neck, barrel chest, and lumbar lordosis.
evidence.explanation: Records the prognathism in the three siblings of the original family.

steps/14.description: Relative prognathism in the original family, secondary to the midface hypoplasia rather than to mandibular overgrowth. Absent in the second patient.

evidence.snippet: craniofacial abnormalities (relative macrocephaly, severe midface hypoplasia with absent nasal cartilage, relative prognathism, and low-set, posteriorly rotated ears) as well as a short neck, barrel chest, and lumbar lordosis.
evidence.explanation: Records the ear position in the three siblings of the original family.

steps/15.description: Low-set and posteriorly rotated in the original family; absent in the second patient, along with the rest of the craniofacial phenotype.

evidence.snippet: craniofacial abnormalities (relative macrocephaly, severe midface hypoplasia with absent nasal cartilage, relative prognathism, and low-set, posteriorly rotated ears) as well as a short neck, barrel chest, and lumbar lordosis.
evidence.explanation: Records the short neck in the three siblings of the original family.

steps/16.description: Part of the axial disproportion in the original family, and consistent with the cervical spine involvement reported there.

evidence.snippet: craniofacial abnormalities (relative macrocephaly, severe midface hypoplasia with absent nasal cartilage, relative prognathism, and low-set, posteriorly rotated ears) as well as a short neck, barrel chest, and lumbar lordosis.
evidence.explanation: Records the chest shape in the three siblings of the original family.

steps/17.description: Reported in the original family. A thoracic manifestation of the spondylar dysplasia rather than a separate lesion.

evidence.snippet: craniofacial abnormalities (relative macrocephaly, severe midface hypoplasia with absent nasal cartilage, relative prognathism, and low-set, posteriorly rotated ears) as well as a short neck, barrel chest, and lumbar lordosis.
evidence.explanation: Records the lumbar lordosis in the three siblings of the original family.

steps/18.description: Reported in the original family. The second patient's spinal curvature was recorded instead as cervical lordosis with thoracolumbar kyphosis, so the axial deformity differs between the two families.

evidence.snippet: The spine showed moderate platyspondyly with cervical lordosis and thoracolumbar kyphosis.
evidence.explanation: Records the thoracolumbar kyphosis in the second patient.

steps/19.description: Recorded in the second patient together with a cervical lordosis, which has no HPO term and so is carried in this description rather than as a separate phenotype. Broken out from the platyspondyly entry because the curvature is a distinct finding from the vertebral body shape.

evidence.snippet: The vertebral endplates were irregular.
evidence.explanation: Records the endplate irregularity in the second patient.

steps/20.description: A radiographic finding in the second patient, and one of the features that placed the phenotype in the SEMD category.

evidence.snippet: The vertebral endplates were irregular. The acetabula were shallow.
evidence.explanation: Records the acetabular dysplasia in the second patient. The preceding sentence is carried with it because the acetabular finding alone is too short to stand as a quotable proposition.

steps/21.description: A radiographic finding in the second patient. Relevant to the degenerative hip disease he went on to develop.

evidence.snippet: Degenerative joint disease of the large joints, particularly of the hip, was significant.
evidence.explanation: Documents the degenerative joint involvement recorded here.

steps/22.description: Premature degenerative joint disease, significant at the hips by middle age in the second patient. It is the expected long-term consequence of a defective articular cartilage matrix, and the reason follow-up in this disease is orthopaedic as much as endocrine.

edges/1.description: The mutant G3 domain was expressed to test whether the substitution acts by disrupting protein production. Shown for the lectin-domain allele only.

edges/2.description: The substitution alters the calcium-coordinating residue in the binding loop. This arm is established for the founding family's p.D2267N allele; the second family's CS-domain variants have not been tested against it.

edges/3.description: Aggrecan that cannot engage its matrix partners normally cannot be integrated into the network the same way.

edges/4.description: Growth-plate cartilage is the template for endochondral bone growth, so a defective matrix there limits linear growth.

edges/5.description: Reduced long bone and vertebral growth.

edges/6.description: Vertebral body growth plates are affected alongside the long bones.

edges/7.description: Disordered metaphyseal modelling.

edges/8.description: The short tubular bones of the hand are affected disproportionately.

edges/9.description: A defective articular cartilage matrix predisposes to premature degenerative joint disease; the intervening years of loading are omitted.

edges/10.description: The growth plates of the limbs are more affected than those of the spine, which is what makes the shortening disproportionate rather than uniform.

edges/11.description: The epiphyseal component of the spondylo-epi-metaphyseal triad, arising at the same secondary ossification centres.

edges/12.description: The cervical vertebral growth plates are affected alongside the rest of the spine.

edges/13.description: The vertebral endplate is a growth plate; its disordered ossification is what the radiographic irregularity records.

edges/14.description: Acetabular deepening is endochondral and follows the same defective cartilage template as the long bones.

edges/15.description: Attributed to the thoracic spondylar and costal dysplasia rather than to a separate lesion. Marked indirect because the intervening rib and sternal mechanics were not studied in either report.

edges/16.description: The cranial base grows by endochondral ossification through the synchondroses, so the same growth-plate defect is the expected route to midface hypoplasia. Marked indirect and unknown-intermediates because neither report examined the cranial base; this is inference from the mechanism, not a measured finding, and the feature is absent in the second patient.

edges/17.description: Ear position is set by the growth of the structures around it, so the low-set, posteriorly rotated ears are carried here as part of the same craniofacial complex. Not separately investigated in either report.

edges/18.description: The macrocephaly is relative: head circumference is preserved while the rest of the skeleton is not, so the disproportion follows from the stature rather than from any additional cranial lesion.

edges/19.description: Wedged and irregular vertebral bodies at the thoracolumbar junction give the segmental kyphosis recorded in the second patient.

edges/20.description: The compensatory lumbar curve recorded in the original family.

edges/21.description: The prognathism is described as relative: the source reports midface hypoplasia with a normally grown mandible, so the jaw position follows from the maxillary deficiency rather than from mandibular overgrowth.

edges/22.description: Acetabular dysplasia concentrates load over a smaller contact area, which is the mechanical route to the hip degeneration that dominated this patient's course. The intervening decades of loading are omitted.

evidence.snippet: These genes were assessed and ranked by cartilage selectivity with whole-genome microarray data, revealing only two genes, encoding aggrecan and chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4, that were selectively expressed in cartilage.
evidence.explanation: Records how ACAN was identified from within the mapped interval, which is what makes the assignment more than positional.

evidence.snippet: At least 25 pathological ACAN mutations have been identified in patients with highly variable phenotypes of syndromic or non-syndromic short stature.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the breadth of the ACAN allelic series, which is the reason this entry states its scope explicitly. Graded OTHER as a review.

evidence.snippet: The variants in the ACAN gene were both missense mutations (c.4138G>T, p.1380V>F, and c.5061T>A, p.1687S>R) and had been tested for mutational effects using the amino acid substitution prediction tool, Mutation Taster
evidence.explanation: Records the second family's two variants in the notation the source uses, together with the fact that their consequence was predicted rather than measured. Quoted verbatim, including the paper's non-standard protein notation, because a curator-normalized form would not be a quote.

evidence.snippet: The patient’s father and mother had already died, and his siblings refused genetic tests; hence, we could not obtain samples from them.
evidence.explanation: Records that phase could not be established for the second family, which is why the recessive assignment there rests on the phenotype and the gene rather than on segregation.

genes/0.notes: Encodes the aggrecan core protein. The recessive disease described here is caused by variants affecting aggrecan: the founding family is homozygous for a G3 C-type lectin domain substitution, and the second patient carries two missense variants in the CS1 and CS2 glycosaminoglycan-attachment domains. ACAN is allelic across a wide range: heterozygous variants cause dominant spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia Kimberley type and familial osteochondritis dissecans, and common variation at the locus associates with normal height. This entry is scoped to the recessive aggrecan-type SEMD and does not absorb those.

evidence.snippet: He underwent surgical correction for genu valgum.
evidence.explanation: The only treatment documented in either report, recorded as what was actually done rather than as a recommendation.

treatments/0.description: Correction of angular deformity such as genu valgum. It addresses the mechanical consequences of disordered growth and does nothing to the matrix defect, which is the only kind of intervention this disease currently has.

evidence.snippet: He underwent surgical correction for genu valgum.
evidence.explanation: Supports the target. Marked INDIRECT because the report records that the operation happened, not a measured outcome from it.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Realigns the limb mechanically. Targeted at the phenotype because the operation acts on the deformity, not on any node in the mechanism.

open_questions/0.rationale: The original siblings reached 66-71 cm; the second patient reached 118.3 cm, had a normal face, and lived independently to 45. That is a very large difference for one ultra-rare Mendelian disorder, and the source does offer an explanation for it: the founding family is homozygous for a C-type lectin domain substitution, the second patient carries two variants in the CS1 and CS2 domains, and the paper states that these different mutation patterns account for the phenotypic difference. The gap is that nothing functional stands behind that attribution. The CS-domain variants were assessed with Mutation Taster and conservation, not expressed or assayed; no comparison against p.D2267N has been made; the parents had died and the siblings refused testing, so the variants could not be shown to be in trans; and the authors' own claim is hedged as speculation. Resolving it needs the same binding and matrix-assembly work that was done for p.D2267N applied to the CS-domain alleles, or a third family. Until then the entry carries a severity range and a domain-location hypothesis, not a genotype-phenotype rule.

open_questions/1.rationale: The binding defect was measured against tenascin-C, and that is the evidence the pathograph carries. But the same domain binds tenascin-R, fibulin-1, fibulin-2 and fibrillin-1 in the same calcium-dependent way, and a calcium-coordinating substitution has no obvious reason to be selective. The entry names tenascin-C because that is what was measured, not because the others were excluded, and this discussion records that distinction so the single-partner framing is not read as an established fact.

evidence.snippet: Hepatorenal tyrosinemia type 1 (HT-1) is a rare autosomal recessive disease that results from a deficiency of fumaryl acetoacetate hydrolase (FAH), a critical enzyme in the catabolic pathway for tyrosine.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports FAH deficiency as the initiating molecular defect.

steps/1.description: Loss of FAH activity blocks the terminal enzymatic step of tyrosine catabolism.

evidence.snippet: This leads to the accumulation of toxic metabolites such as fumaryl and maleylacetoacetate, which can damage the liver, kidneys, and nervous system.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports toxic-metabolite accumulation downstream of FAH deficiency.

steps/2.description: FAH deficiency causes accumulation of fumarylacetoacetate (FAA) and maleylacetoacetate (MAA), with secondary formation of succinylacetone (SA). These toxic tyrosine-pathway metabolites damage the liver, kidneys, and nervous system, and FAA directly triggers mitochondrial cytochrome c release in hepatocytes.

evidence.snippet: Our data indicate that succinylacetone is an extremely potent competitive inhibitor of ALA dehydratase in human as well as in animal tissues.
evidence.explanation: Biochemical evidence directly supports succinylacetone inhibition of ALA dehydratase.

evidence.snippet: patients with this hereditary disease excrete excessive amounts of delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) in urine and that certain patients have an accompanying clinical syndrome resembling that of acute intermittent porphyria (AIP).
evidence.explanation: Patient observations connect HT-1 to ALA accumulation and porphyria-like neurovisceral crises.

evidence.snippet: In cultured hepatocytes, succinylacetone also inhibited ALA dehydratase activity, decreased the cellular content of heme and cytochrome P-450
evidence.explanation: Supports reduced heme-biosynthesis output downstream of succinylacetone-mediated ALAD inhibition.

steps/3.description: Succinylacetone (SA) is a competitive inhibitor of delta-aminolevulinic acid dehydratase (ALAD), blocking the heme biosynthetic pathway and causing accumulation of delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA). This produces porphyria-like neurovisceral crises with neuropathy, similar to acute intermittent porphyria or lead poisoning.

evidence.snippet: Cytochrome c was released from mitochondria prior to liver failure in the Fah-/- Hpd-/- double-mutant mice after the administration of HGA. In a cell-free system, the addition of fumarylacetoacetate induced the release of cytochrome c from the mitochondria.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that FAA directly induces mitochondrial cytochrome c release in tyrosinemia model.

evidence.snippet: We also found that caspase inhibitors were highly effective in preventing the liver failure induced by HGA in the double-mutant mice.
evidence.explanation: Proves caspase-mediated apoptosis is the mechanism of hepatocyte injury in tyrosinemia.

steps/4.description: Fumarylacetoacetate directly triggers mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization with release of cytochrome c, activating the caspase cascade and inducing hepatocyte apoptosis. Caspase inhibitors were shown to prevent liver failure in FAH-deficient mouse models, confirming the causal role of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway.

evidence.snippet: This leads to the accumulation of toxic metabolites such as fumaryl and maleylacetoacetate, which can damage the liver, kidneys, and nervous system.
evidence.explanation: Directly links toxic metabolite accumulation to kidney injury in HT-1.

steps/5.description: Accumulated tyrosine-pathway metabolites injure kidney tissue, especially the proximal tubule, causing a Fanconi-like renal phenotype with phosphate wasting. This renal tubular mechanism explains renal tubular dysfunction and secondary hypophosphatemic rickets in HT-1.

evidence.snippet: Undiagnosed and untreated tyrosinemia type 1 (TT1) individuals carry a significant risk for developing liver fibrosis, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
evidence.explanation: Directly links untreated HT-1 to fibrosis, cirrhosis, and HCC.

evidence.snippet: The differentially expressed genes were enriched in toxicological gene classes related to liver disease, liver damage, liver regeneration and liver cancer, in particular HCC.
evidence.explanation: Mouse transcriptomics supports persistent hepatic injury, regeneration, and HCC-related programs under NTBC.

steps/6.description: Untreated or late-treated HT-1 produces chronic hepatic injury with regeneration, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and malignant transformation risk. Continuous NTBC reduces acute toxicity but does not restore FAH activity, so residual liver-disease and HCC-associated programs can persist.

evidence.snippet: The differentially expressed genes were enriched in toxicological gene classes related to liver disease, liver damage, liver regeneration and liver cancer, in particular HCC.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates persistent HCC-related gene expression under NTBC therapy in mouse model.

evidence.snippet: NTBC does not restore the enzymatic defects inflicted by the disease nor does it cure HT1.
evidence.explanation: Confirms NTBC does not cure the underlying enzymatic deficiency.

steps/7.description: Although nitisinone prevents acute toxicity by blocking upstream toxic metabolite formation, it does not restore FAH activity. Transcriptomic analysis in FAH-deficient mice under continuous NTBC revealed persistent enrichment of genes related to liver disease, liver regeneration, and hepatocellular carcinoma. This supports the ongoing HCC risk even in treated patients.

evidence.snippet: Tyrosinemia type I (hepatorenal tyrosinemia, HT-1) is an autosomal recessive condition resulting in hepatic failure with comorbidities involving the renal and neurologic systems
evidence.explanation: Directly supports hepatic failure as a primary manifestation.

evidence.snippet: Patients failing medical treatment (eg, due to non-adherence), and who develop acute liver failure (ALF), have HCC or evidence of histologically proven dysplastic liver nodule(s)
evidence.explanation: Confirms acute liver failure as an indication for liver transplantation in HT-1.

steps/8.description: Acute hepatic decompensation is a hallmark of untreated or severe HT-1, driven by FAA-mediated oxidative damage and caspase-dependent apoptosis of hepatocytes. In untreated acute-form HT-1, liver failure typically presents in the first months of life.

evidence.snippet: Undiagnosed and untreated tyrosinemia type 1 (TT1) individuals carry a significant risk for developing liver fibrosis, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
evidence.explanation: Directly lists liver fibrosis as a significant risk in untreated HT-1.

steps/9.description: Progressive liver fibrosis and cirrhosis develop in untreated or late-treated HT-1. Even false-negative NBS cases have presented with cirrhosis years later.

evidence.snippet: A nine-year-old boy presented with HCC in a cirrhotic liver.
evidence.explanation: Documents cirrhosis in a missed NBS case of HT-1.

evidence.snippet: A liver biopsy confirmed mixed nodular cirrhosis, and a subsequent whole exome sequencing revealed autosomal recessive inheritance of tyrosinemia type 1.
evidence.explanation: Confirms cirrhosis in a late-presenting HT-1 patient.

steps/10.description: Cirrhosis develops progressively in untreated HT-1 as a consequence of chronic hepatocyte injury and regeneration. A case of false-negative NBS presented at age 9 with HCC in a cirrhotic liver.

evidence.snippet: NTBC combined with dietary therapy, if initiated early, can provide liver transplant (LT) free survival and reduce the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
evidence.explanation: Confirms HCC as a recognized risk requiring monitoring.

steps/11.description: HCC is the most feared long-term complication of HT-1. Risk persists even under NTBC therapy, necessitating lifelong surveillance with alpha-fetoprotein monitoring and liver imaging.

evidence.snippet: This leads to the accumulation of toxic metabolites such as fumaryl and maleylacetoacetate, which can damage the liver, kidneys, and nervous system.
